Yes, Joule Work desktop is secure. Key security measures include:

  • Encrypted local storage: Conversations are stored on your device in an AES-256 encrypted database, with encryption keys stored in your OS keychain.

  • Sandboxed file access: Joule can only read or write files within your selected working directory.

  • Approval gates: Joule always asks before writing files or running terminal commands.

  • Secure credential storage: OAuth tokens and API keys are stored via OS-level secure storage.

Joule Work desktop can automate these tasks:

  • Running scripts (Python, Node, shell commands) in your working directory.

  • Reading, writing, editing, and organizing local files.

  • Searching your email and summarizing inbox content.

  • Pulling calendar data and surfacing schedule insights.

  • Calling external systems via connectors (APIs, databases, third-party tools).

  • Chaining multi-step workflows using skills.

Connectors in Joule Work desktop are built on the MCP (Model Context Protocol) standard. They let Joule connect to external systems—like Jira, databases, or custom APIs—so it can read data, write data, and trigger actions directly from the chat. Users can add connectors, each of which exposes a set of tools that Joule can use in conversation. Authentication supports no-auth, bearer token, or OAuth 2.0.

You can automate anything that involves combining file work, code execution, and external system calls. Examples include:

  • Pulling data from a connector, processing it with a Python script, and saving a formatted report to your working directory.

  • Searching your inbox for emails on a topic, summarizing them, and drafting a response.

  • Running a multi-step analysis across several local documents and outputting results to a new file.

  • Using a skill to standardize a repeatable workflow like weekly status reports, content briefs, and more.

Once you give Joule Work desktop access to a folder on your machine, it can read, write, edit and search files across that folder. Joule will ask for your approval before making any changes.

Joule Work desktop can work with images and documents up to 10 MB, it can work with any file type that Joule can read or generate, including text files, code, CSVs, JSON, Markdown, Office, and PDF documents. It can also create new files as output from a task.

FAQ

A tabular foundation model (TFM) is a pretrained AI model designed to understand rows, columns, and relationships in structured data to enable predictions across tasks without training a separate model.

Unlike large language models, which process text by converting data into a single sequence of tokens, tabular foundation models like SAP-RPT are designed to preserve relationships within structured data from sources such as sales records or supplier-performance transactions. This enables more accurate AI outputs and predictions in the context of a specific business domain, activity, and process.

In-context learning allows the SAP-RPT model to understand patterns on the fly and quickly adapt to new scenarios from example records included in your API call. Context registry and selection help identify the most relevant tables and columns to generate accurate predictions.

Yes, you can test the latest version of SAP-RPT for free at the SAP-RPT playground or through the SAP AI Core trial. Configure prediction scenarios, evaluate model performance, generate predictions, explore the rows and columns that explain prediction outcomes, and interact with your data in natural language. Yes. open-source versions of SAP-RPT are available on Hugging Face and GitHub for research and non-commercial purposes. Commercial versions are available to customers through the model library in SAP AI Core.

The tabular orchestration workflow automates specialized tabular and predictive capabilities for the SAP-RPT tabular foundation model. Tabular orchestration is delivered on SAP AI Core, accessible via APIs, and it includes out of the box integration across data sources, context registration, selection, and management. The new workflow option removes the need for manual context engineering and model handling by automatically selecting the right context, building the API call, and returning predictions based on query rows provided at runtime.

A model card is standardized technical documentation that describes a tabular foundational model purpose, capabilities, intended uses, evaluation results, limitations, and responsible-use considerations. It helps technical and business users assess whether a model is appropriate for a specific use case and deploy it with appropriate safeguards.

Frequently asked questions

Tabular AI applies machine learning to structured data, or the rows and columns across enterprise data sources that power most business decisions. Organizations are building a strategy around it today because tabular foundation models (TFMs) make it practical to generate accurate predictions at scale, without requiring dedicated model training for every use case. Tabular AI on SAP goes further, bringing TFMs and large language models (LLMs) together with orchestration, centralized management, and governance through a single AI service.

Tabular foundation models are AI systems pretrained on large, structured datasets to learn common tabular data patterns. Unlike LLMs, which are trained on text, tabular foundation models operate natively on rows and columns, fully understanding the rich semantics and relationships in structured data. As fully managed, pretrained models, TFMs eliminate the need for custom training, accelerating time to value while reducing cost and complexity.

A prediction is the statistical output of a tabular AI model. A predictive insight adapts that prediction to prompt users to act with increased precision, based on a complete understanding of the semantics and relationships in your structured data. Tabular AI on SAP goes further by operationalizing predictions and insights with specialized capabilities, such as tabular orchestration, context selection, and registry, that increase the contextualization and reasoning of the AI models based on your business data. products/artificial-intelligence/what-is.description: Artificial intelligence (AI), or simply AI, is the simulation of human intelligence in machines. Learn how AI works, its types, real-world applications, and future challenges.
products/artificial-intelligence/what-is.body:
What Is

What is artificial intelligence?

Artificial intelligence (AI) is the simulation of human intelligence by computers and machines—enabling them to learn from data, reason, solve problems, and perform tasks that typically require human intelligence.

Updated on January 26, 2026

What are the origins and history of AI?

Artificial intelligence refers to computer systems built to perform tasks that traditionally require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, pattern recognition, problem-solving, and decision-making. AI underpins many of today’s most transformative digital experiences, from real-time translation and recommendations to automation, voice assistants, and predictive business analytics.

The vision of intelligent machines has roots in philosophy and mathematics. The term "artificial intelligence" originated in 1956 at a scientific conference held at Dartmouth College. One of AI’s founding fathers, Marvin Minsky, described it as “the science of making machines do things that would require intelligence if done by men.” Modern AI has rapidly accelerated thanks to pioneers like Alan Turing, who introduced the “Turing Test” for machine intelligence, and John McCarthy, who coined the term “artificial intelligence” and established its study as a scientific field in the 1950s. Since then, advances in computing, data, and algorithm design have taken AI from theory to practice, transforming nearly every industry and facet of daily life.

Types and levels of AI

Artificial intelligence comes in several forms, each defined by its capabilities and the ways it supports humans in solving real-world problems. Today’s most powerful business AI solutions—such as those found in SAP applications—are focused on narrowly defined tasks, including predicting demand, recognizing images, or automating repetitive processes. These systems work in tandem with employees, enhancing productivity, reducing errors, and providing the insights necessary for informed decision-making.​

AI by capability

More general or autonomous forms of AI, which could theoretically match or surpass a human’s broad intelligence, remain the subject of academic research and responsible debate. Understanding how AI complements human strengths can help organizations adopt these technologies responsibly and achieve meaningful outcomes. The table below breaks down the main types and levels of AI, showing where today’s capabilities deliver proven business value.​

Level

Description

Business use

Narrow AI

Performs specific tasks with intelligence

Chatbots, recommendation engines

General AI

Would mimic full human cognitive abilities

Not yet realized

Narrow AI

The most common type encountered in daily life and business is narrow AI, also known as weak AI. These systems tackle specific tasks, such as recognizing speech, analyzing images, and making recommendations. In business, narrow AI powers chatbots, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation, helping to drive efficiency and accuracy in complex processes.​

General AI

General AI represents a theoretical future where machines could seamlessly adapt, learn, and reason across any field, matching the breadth of human intelligence. While ongoing research explores what might be possible, general AI does not exist today. Instead, advances in deep learning and data integration continue to expand the capabilities of specialized AI systems.​

Types of AI functionality

AI can also be categorized by how it processes information, from simple rule-based reactive systems to adaptive agents with memory, prediction, and collaboration capabilities. Each type brings different strengths and use cases to industries, from autonomous robots in manufacturing to advanced fraud detection in finance.

The table below explains how these types and levels of AI are applied in practical business applications today.

Type

Example/use case

Reactive

Rule-based assistants, basic chatbots

Limited memory

Predictive maintenance, forecasting

Theory of mind*

Empathy, advanced sentiment analysis

Self-aware*

Would be capable of autonomous self-reasoning

*Primarily theoretical today.

How does artificial intelligence work?

AI uses large datasets to identify patterns, learn from experience, and make informed decisions. In a business context, data is collected and used to train an AI model; the trained model is then deployed for AI inference—meaning it applies what it has learned to new, unseen data to generate predictions or decisions in real-world conditions with speed, precision, and adaptability.

Machine learning

Machine learning models learn from historical data and improve over time, identifying trends and making predictions.

Deep learning

Deep learning uses complex neural networks to recognize patterns in images, speech, or other data, enabling applications such as image recognition and voice assistants.

Neural networks

Neural networks are a specific type of machine learning architecture that excels at processing vast and complex datasets. They power sophisticated solutions for forecasting, customer insights, risk analysis, and personalization.

Natural language processing (NLP)

NLP enables computers to understand and respond to human language, facilitating the development of intelligent chatbots and language translation systems.

Generative AI

Generative AI creates new content, such as text, images, or code, based on prompts, enabling next-generation creativity and productivity.

AI inference

AI inference refers to the process of applying a trained AI model to fresh, real-world data in order to generate predictions or classifications in business workflows. For example, after a neural network is trained on historic sales or transaction data, it can infer likely outcomes for new sales leads or detect anomalies as they occur, driving operational efficiency and better decision-making.

Discover the value of trusted data in AI success

Discover how unified, governed data from SAP enables smarter analytics, planning, and AI at scale—enabling organizations to transform insights into tangible business impact.

Explore data management

AI applications

Artificial intelligence powers a diverse range of applications, enabling businesses to operate faster, smarter, and more resiliently through automation, prediction, and enhanced experiences.​

Everyday examples

These points demonstrate how AI already appears in everyday tools and services people use at home and at work, often without them realizing it is AI-supported.

  • Digital assistants
    Voice-powered tools like Siri, Alexa, and Google Assistant help with reminders, scheduling, and hands-free device control, streamlining both work and home routines.​
  • Personalized recommendations
    Streaming platforms (Netflix, Spotify) and online retailers use AI to analyze past behavior, offering product and content suggestions tailored to each user.​
  • Image recognition and OCR
    AI systems recognize objects, translate street signs, perform facial recognition for security, and extract text/data from photos or scanned documents.​
  • Autonomous systems
    Self-parking and driver-assist features in cars, warehouse robots, and delivery drones use AI to interpret their surroundings and react in real time.​
  • Chatbots and virtual agents
    Many websites and apps use AI-driven chatbots to answer questions, resolve support issues, and handle routine customer needs 24/7.​
  • Smart home automation
    Thermostats, lighting, and security systems adjust automatically by learning from daily behaviors, contributing to convenience, comfort, and energy savings.​

Core business functions

The following bullets outline how AI supports core business processes, helping teams work faster, reduce errors, and make more informed decisions.

  • Finance: Automate invoice matching, transaction monitoring, fraud detection, risk assessment, and financial forecasting. Machine learning models streamline closing cycles and support audit compliance.​
  • Supply chain and logistics: Power demand forecasting, real-time inventory management, delivery route optimization, quality inspections, and predictive maintenance to help avoid shortages, excesses, and costly downtime.​
  • Procurement: Enhance supplier performance and compliance, automate sourcing, and optimize spend analysis using AI-supported intelligent recommendations and anomaly detection.​
  • Sales and marketing: Personalize customer journeys, drive campaign targeting, and optimize pricing models by analyzing large volumes of customer and market data.​
  • Human resources: Accelerate talent acquisition with AI-driven candidate screening, predict attrition, and support employee engagement and personalized learning.​
  • Customer experience: Deploy conversational AI, chatbots, and recommendation engines to provide fast, personalized assistance and boost satisfaction.​

Industry-specific examples

These examples illustrate how different industries apply AI to solve domain-specific challenges, from equipment reliability to patient care.

  • Manufacturing
    Predict equipment failures before they happen, optimize production lines, enable real-time supply/demand planning, and increase traceability with computer vision and IoT-enabled AI.​
  • Retail
    Facilitate hyper-personalized product offers, automate inventory replenishment, and analyze customer feedback for continuous improvement.​
  • Healthcare
    Support diagnostics, resource scheduling, and personalized treatment recommendations using AI-based analysis of patient data.​
  • Utilities and energy
    Forecast demand, reduce outages, optimize energy distribution, and analyze infrastructure conditions to inform decisions.​

Everyday enterprise applications

The points below focus on common, cross-cutting AI use cases that can be deployed in almost any organization to streamline knowledge work and operations.

  • Document processing
    AI can extract and classify data from invoices, contracts, and reports, reducing manual entry, improving accuracy, and speeding compliance checks.
  • Intelligent search and smart data extraction
    Instantly locate relevant information and files within vast digital archives, empowering faster, more confident decisions across business functions.
  • Automated incident management and IT operations
    AI monitors systems continuously, detects anomalies, and handles incidents automatically to keep critical business applications stable and secure around the clock.
  • Natural language queries
    Users can simply ask business questions in plain language (such as “Show last month’s top-performing products”) and receive immediate insights or visualizations, democratizing access to analytics.
  • Anomaly detection
    AI identifies unusual patterns in transactions, system logs, or user behaviors, supporting fraud prevention, risk management, and early alerting for operations teams.
  • Workflow automation
    From routing customer requests to scheduling maintenance, AI-enhanced automation ensures the right processes run smoothly with minimal manual oversight.

These applications drive smarter, faster, and more reliable outcomes while freeing people to focus on higher-value, creative, and strategic work.

Benefits of AI

Artificial intelligence delivers significant value across industries by transforming productivity, decision-making, customer experiences, and operational outcomes:​

  • Automation and productivity
    AI automates routine tasks such as data entry, invoice processing, and report generation, freeing employees to focus on higher-value strategic work and increasing business productivity.
  • Improved decision-making
    AI-enhanced analytics and predictive models enable faster, more accurate decisions for demand forecasting, financial planning, and risk management, allowing organizations to anticipate market changes and respond proactively.
  • Enhanced customer experience
    Intelligent chatbots, recommendation engines, and personalized interfaces strengthen engagement, speed service response, and help brands build stronger relationships with customers.
  • Cost savings and efficiency
    By optimizing operations such as supply chain management, HR, and procurement, AI can help reduce operational costs, minimize waste, and drive more efficient resource allocation.
  • Innovation and agility
    AI enables organizations to experiment rapidly, support new product launches, and adapt processes swiftly in response to changing market and customer needs.
  • Collaboration and knowledge sharingAI-enhanced tools facilitate cross-team collaboration, making critical information and insights accessible to all key stakeholders.

AI ethics and challenges

As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in businesses and daily life, it brings both opportunities and responsibilities. Addressing the ethical considerations of AI is essential to ensure technologies remain trustworthy, fair, and secure. Responsible AI design answers key questions such as “Is AI safe?” and “What are the main ethical concerns businesses and society must consider as AI evolves?”

The adoption of AI presents several complex ethical considerations and practical challenges for businesses and society:​

  • Bias and fairness
    AI models can perpetuate and amplify existing biases in training data, potentially leading to unfair outcomes in hiring, lending, or resource allocation. Addressing bias requires ongoing testing, diverse data sources, and transparent development practices.
  • Transparency and explainability
    Many AI algorithms, especially deep learning models, operate as black boxes, making it difficult for users to understand how decisions are made. Building systems that offer clear explanations helps establish trust and regulatory compliance.
  • Data privacy and security
    AI systems often rely on vast amounts of data, raising concerns about privacy, consent, and information security. Companies must establish robust data governance frameworks and comply with regional data regulations.
  • Safety and deepfakes
    Powerful generative AI can create hyper-realistic but fake images, audio, or video (deepfakes), fueling misinformation and risks to privacy, democracy, and brand reputation.
  • Regulation and compliance
    Laws and standards governing AI continue to evolve globally. Staying ahead of regulations helps protect businesses from legal exposure and reinforces ethical use.

Organizations must foster a culture of responsible AI, implementing fair, transparent, and accountable practices while proactively monitoring risks and continuously adapting to the advancement of technologies and evolving societal expectations.

FAQs

  • What’s the difference between AI and machine learning?

    AI is a broad field focused on empowering machines to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, or problem-solving. Within AI, machine learning refers to systems that learn from data over time, without explicit programming for every outcome. In SAP solutions, machine learning powers practical automation, from invoice processing to predictive analytics, helping organizations continuously refine their decisions and workflows.

  • What is artificial intelligence in simple terms?

    AI is when computers are designed to learn from data and solve problems much like humans do—by recognizing patterns, making decisions, and even adapting as they gain more experience. Today, AI powers everyday technologies such as digital assistants, recommendation systems, and smart chatbots, helping organizations automate routine work and deliver faster, more intelligent service. For a deeper look at how AI works in business and the many real-world benefits, see SAP's guide to AI.

  • What are the four types of AI?

    AI takes many forms, including rule-based systems, machine learning models, deep learning, and generative AI. SAP Business AI embeds industry-specific capabilities to match business needs: conversational bots for customer support, predictive models for supply chain forecasting, and generative AI for content creation. Explore SAP’s Business AI portfolio to see which type best suits your process or workflow.

  • What are common examples of AI?

    Organizations across every sector utilize AI to enhance productivity and accuracy. For example, retailers optimize inventory and pricing using demand forecasting, while HR teams utilize AI-driven talent matching and sentiment analysis. Manufacturers, in turn, employ predictive maintenance to reduce downtime. See more SAP Business AI use cases for tailored industry scenarios and business outcomes.

  • What are the benefits of using AI in business?

    AI drives tangible business results, including increased speed, precision, cost savings, and improved customer and employee experiences. SAP embeds AI directly into its applications, enabling decision-makers to act quickly and confidently with data-driven insights.

  • Is AI good or bad?

    AI adoption necessitates responsible governance, addressing challenges such as bias, privacy, transparency, and regulatory compliance. SAP’s approach prioritizes ethical design, robust security, and explainability, ensuring that every AI solution supports fair and accountable decisions that build trust with stakeholders. Learn best practices for responsible AI in SAP, including the use of transparent algorithms and continuous monitoring for identifying new risks.

SAP Commerce Cloud is SAP's enterprise e-commerce solution designed to help companies of any size adapt to changing business needs. Supporting B2B, B2C, and B2B2C commerce, it enables organizations to deliver personalized omnichannel experiences; manage complex catalogs, products, and configurations; and scale commerce operations as customer expectations and business requirements evolve.

No, SAP Commerce Cloud is not a standalone CRM. It is a digital commerce solution within the SAP Customer Experience portfolio that enables online selling, product discovery, pricing, promotions, and order management. SAP Commerce Cloud can integrate with CRM and customer data solutions to help businesses deliver personalized customer journeys.

SAP Commerce Cloud is the evolution of SAP Hybris. While "SAP Hybris" was the historic product name, SAP Commerce Cloud is the current cloud-based commerce solution that includes AI-powered capabilities, cloud delivery, and integration with SAP's broader business applications. Organizations researching SAP Hybris today should evaluate SAP Commerce Cloud.

SAP Commerce Cloud helps simplify e-commerce operations by delivering a seamless customer experience from product discovery to purchase. A combination of self-service capabilities, AI-enhanced merchandising, guided selling, assisted service, and chatbots helps improve customer engagement and increase efficiency. The platform also streamlines complex commerce and order processes, helping businesses connect demand with inventory, fulfillment, and supply chain operations.

Prebuilt integration is based on SAP Integration Suite, which helps connect SAP Commerce Cloud with other SAP and third-party applications. Since SAP Commerce Cloud is based on open APIs, you can quickly integrate it with third-party solutions as well. We offer many prebuilt integrations through SAP Store. You can also use serverless microservices to extend your e-commerce architecture through the open-source project “Kyma.”

Yes, SAP Commerce Cloud supports headless commerce through an API-first approach and the decoupled JavaScript-based storefront layer. This approach gives businesses the flexibility to create and manage commerce experiences across websites, mobile apps, devices, and digital channels without changing the core commerce platform.

Yes, SAP Commerce Cloud provides an embedded solution for PIM through SAP Product Content Management, part of the SAP Commerce Cloud portfolio.

 

Product Content Management enables you to consolidate product data and catalogs centrally and publish them through various channels. You can make edits through an intuitive user interface, enhance product content quality with built-in data validation and workflows, bulk edit and mass upload product data, and support multilingual catalogs for a global e-commerce site.

A unified commerce solution is a platform that connects every commerce touchpoint—online storefronts, in-store, mobile, and marketplaces—with the back-office systems that run the business—inventory, pricing, order management, and customer data. Rather than managing separate systems for each channel, a unified commerce platform gives businesses a single, real-time foundation that delivers consistent experiences wherever customers engage. It also creates the connected data foundation that AI needs to act reliably across the commerce lifecycle.

These terms describe distinct but related concepts:

  • Unified commerce is the infrastructure layer, connecting channels, inventory, pricing, orders, and customer data into a single, connected platform.

  • Agentic commerce refers to AI agents acting on behalf of buyers to discover products, compare options, and assist in completing transactions.

  • Autonomous unified commerce goes beyond helping customers find and buy products. It enables AI to continuously optimize how commerce operates, from product discovery and demand generation to inventory, fulfillment, pricing, and customer engagement, driving better outcomes with every interaction.

SAP brings all three together on a single data foundation.

 

Unified commerce platforms eliminate the silos that cause inconsistent experiences and missed revenue:

  • Consistent experiences across every channel—same pricing, availability, and service.

  • Real-time inventory visibility for accurate availability and faster fulfillment.

  • Centralized product and order data that reduces manual effort and errors.

  • A reliable AI foundation—agents need connected, real-time data to act reliably.

  • B2B, B2C, and B2B2C support on a single platform.

Explore unified commerce to see these benefits in action.

 

SAP Commerce Cloud delivers capabilities across the full commerce lifecycle:

  • AI-powered merchandising—optimize product content for AI search, SEO, and storefronts.

  • Personalized experiences—adapt in real time to customer intent and history to drive conversion.

  • Connected order management—fulfill every order accurately with real-time inventory and pricing.

  • Continuous optimization—improve assortment, reduce costs, and grow customer lifetime value.

These capabilities are all made possible by role-based assistants such as Merchandising Assistant, Shopping Assistant, and Order Management Assistant. See all AI assistants for SAP CX.

 

SAP Commerce Cloud supports B2B, B2C, and B2B2C on a single platform. For B2C, that means personalized storefronts, AI-driven discovery, promotions, and high-volume order handling. For B2B, it means account-based pricing, contract management, guided selling, approval workflows, and automated replenishment. Both models share the same connected data foundation—real-time inventory, pricing, and customer context—so AI acts reliably across buyer types. Explore SAP Commerce Cloud.

Most platforms optimize individual touchpoints. SAP is the only vendor connecting SAP Commerce Cloud, order management, ERP, supply chain, and loyalty on a single data foundation. That means AI agents have full business context—not just storefront data—to make decisions grounded in operational reality. You can promise what you can actually deliver, and every interaction becomes a signal that makes the next decision better.

A customer engagement platform is a solution that connects customer data, marketing automation, and omnichannel execution to deliver personalized interactions. It gives businesses a single foundation to orchestrate relevant experiences throughout the customer lifecycle so teams don’t have to manage disconnected tools for each channel or audience. It also creates the connected data foundation that agentic AI needs to act reliably on customer and business signals.

A customer engagement platform eliminates the silos that cause disconnected experiences and missed revenue opportunities. It provides:

  • Personalized interactions across every channel, grounded in unified customer and business data.

  • Real-time engagement with customer and business signals, so every interaction is timely and relevant.

  • Alignment for marketing and sales teams working from a shared real-time view of the customer.

  • Built-in security, governance, and compliance, giving AI tools the trusted foundation to personalize and automate at scale.

  • B2B and B2C support on a single composable platform.

Designed for retail, consumer products, travel, and hospitality, SAP Engagement Cloud drives relevant, trusted engagement at scale to improve conversion, strengthen loyalty, and increase customer lifetime value.

Yes, SAP provides B2B marketing solutions that help organizations engage multiple stakeholders, build business relationships, and support complex buying journeys.

 

SAP Engagement Cloud connects enterprise data with marketing, sales, service, and commerce processes, aligning teams around a shared view of the customer to deliver personalized engagement across the customer lifecycle.

 

Joule coordinates AI agents to identify high-value accounts, personalize content, surface cross-sell and up-sell opportunities, and drive retention and long-term account growth.

Most customer engagement solutions draw from siloed customer data, separate from commerce, sales, service, and ERP. SAP Engagement Cloud connects them on a single data foundation. That gives AI agents live business context—inventory, order history, service cases—when deciding what to send, when to send it, and to whom. The result is engagement built on operational truth to create more opportunities to grow revenue.

SAP Sales Cloud gives sales teams a real-time view of their pipeline by bringing opportunities, forecasts, customer interactions, and AI-enhanced insights together in one place. Sales managers can identify at-risk deals, monitor pipeline health, track performance, and make more informed decisions to improve forecast accuracy and increase win rates.

SAP Sales Cloud has autonomous AI agents that help automate lead qualification, opportunity management, meeting preparation, quote creation, email insights, pipeline risk analysis, and other routine sales tasks. These capabilities help sales teams work more efficiently, make faster decisions, and focus on selling.

SAP Sales Cloud can help you improve forecast accuracy, identify at-risk opportunities, and increase win rates with embedded AI that provides recommendations on what tasks or interactions should be performed to increase forecast accuracy. The embedded AI performs continuous correlation analysis to identify links between seller behavior, opportunity win rate, and other complex variables. This allows sales managers to assess forecast accuracy and model various potential outcomes with data-driven analysis of propensity to close.

SAP Sales Cloud includes specialized "perfect store” functionality to help you create retail execution action plans, optimize visit logistics, and improve the efficiency of on-site activities. Dynamic visit surveys and planograms guide retail execution activities while unifying store audit information to enable continuous improvement of retail execution at each location. Unified KPIs provide insight into year-over-year improvement and can be used to improve resource allocation, execution strategy, and store performance across extended distribution networks.

SAP Sales Cloud can help you identify actionable customer insights by centralizing critical data for a full view of each account. Embedded sales intelligence surfaces critical data automatically and enables real-time exploration of the customer journey through each stage of the sales pipeline. Meanwhile, intuitive visualizations can provide valuable buying journey insights and help business users identify and proactively solve sales process breakdowns.

Yes, SAP Sales Cloud connects with SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA to bring sales, customer, and operational data together in a single workflow. This gives sales teams direct access to customer accounts, product availability, pricing, quotes, orders, and order status without jumping between systems. This product integration helps drive greater productivity, lessen manual effort, and deliver more connected customer experiences.

B2B selling has become increasingly complex, and leading organizations are helping sales teams improve outcomes by providing prescriptive guidance for opportunity progression. Guided selling functionality within SAP Sales Cloud provides a framework to help you understand and respond to customer needs with an interactive, value-driven approach that's shaped by real-time data.

Yes, organizations can leverage dynamic visit planning functionality within SAP Sales Cloud to help reduce overhead and improve efficiency of store and site visit logistics, scheduling, and routing. Embedded intelligence utilizes real-time and historical data to dynamically optimize how and when field sales and retail execution staff visit customer locations.

SAP Sales Cloud supports organizations across a wide range of industries, including manufacturing, consumer products, retail, wholesale distribution, automotive, high tech, life sciences, and professional services. It helps businesses manage complex sales processes, strengthen customer relationships, and improve sales performance regardless of industry.

Yes, SAP Sales Cloud is available on mobile devices, enabling sales teams to access customer information, manage opportunities, update activities, capture meeting notes, and stay productive from anywhere. With online and offline capabilities, sales representatives can continue working even when connectivity is limited and sync their updates once they're back online.

Customer service software helps businesses manage customer interactions across multiple channels, including phone, email, chat, and social media.

When evaluating customer service software, consider your current support volume and channels, integration requirements with existing systems, scalability needs as your business grows, and budget constraints. Key factors to look for include omnichannel capabilities to meet customers where they are, AI and automation features to improve efficiency, reporting and analytics for performance insights, and ease of use for your team. It’s also important to assess whether the solution can connect customer service data with other business functions like sales and operations for a complete customer view.

SAP Service Cloud distinguishes itself through deep integration with enterprise systems, making it well suited for organizations already using SAP or complex ERP environments. Unlike standalone platforms that focus on ticketing and communication, SAP Service Cloud connects service data with broader business processes, giving agents real-time visibility and the ability to act without switching systems. Designed for mid-to-large enterprises, SAP Service Cloud combines case management, knowledge base functionality, and AI-enhanced automation to support efficient issue resolution while maintaining a complete customer view.

AI is embedded throughout SAP Service Cloud to automate routine tasks, enhance agent productivity, and improve the customer experience. Current AI capabilities include email and case summaries, a generative AI email drafter, intelligent recommendations, and sentiment analysis, helping service teams work more efficiently and consistently.

SAP Service Cloud’s AI is built with SAP Business AI, which is trained on decades of enterprise business process data across industries. Unlike generic AI tools, it understands business context and integrates with SAP's broader ecosystem including CRM, ERP, and commerce systems. This allows for AI-driven recommendations based on complete, trusted business data rather than isolated service interactions. Embedded throughout the service journey, SAP Service Cloud’s AI helps automate processes, accelerate resolution, and support service agents with relevant, reliable insights.

FAQ

A business data fabric is an architecture that connects data and context in one governed foundation, serving as the trusted knowledge core for every enterprise application and AI agent. Unlike traditional data management approaches, a business data fabric preserves the meaning behind your data by design, making it foundational for scalable, trustworthy AI. It brings together critical capabilities such as data integration, lakehouse, data products, data marketplace, semantics, knowledge graphs, and modeling into a unified platform without compromising architectural flexibility.

A data fabric connects and manages distributed data across complex landscapes. A business data fabric goes further by preserving the business context behind that data, including its semantics, policies, and business processes. This gives applications and AI agents consistent access to data with the meaning needed to generate trusted insights and actions.

A knowledge core connects semantics, trusted entities, relationships, metadata, ontologies, and business rules to provide a shared business context for analytics and AI. Unlike a static semantic layer, it is continuously enriched by how data is used across domains and use cases, incorporating new relationships, decisions, and process logic as the business evolves. The knowledge core gives AI agents a consistent and adaptive understanding of how the business operates, helping them reason and act with greater context and alignment.

A business data fabric gives agents governed access to organizational data with the business context needed to understand relationships, reason across domains, and take informed action. By grounding agents in shared semantics, enterprise knowledge, and real-time data, this architectural approach enables more trusted and coordinated AI-driven decisions and workflows.

A data lake or data warehouse stores and organizes data, but it does not preserve the business context around it. A business data fabric goes further by connecting that context across your entire landscape, making data not just accessible but interpretable. This distinction becomes critical when AI systems need to make autonomous decisions that align with real business outcomes.

A semantic layer gives data consistent business meaning by defining shared metrics, relationships, and business logic across domains. Within a business data fabric, it connects these semantics with data models, ontologies, and knowledge graphs so analytics, applications, and AI can interpret and use data consistently across various use cases.

SAP Business Data Cloud, a key component of SAP Business AI Platform, is anchored in a business data fabric that delivers universal business context and serves as the trusted knowledge core for every enterprise application and agent. This knowledge core brings together SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP Master Data Governance, and SAP Reltio to unify SAP and third-party data, including SAP Business Warehouse, under enterprise-wide governance so that every AI initiative operates from the same trusted foundation.

 

The SAP business data fabric runs on intelligent compute, giving customers flexibility to run best-of-breed compute for every data and AI workload based on business demands with SAP HANA Cloud, SAP Databricks, and the SAP Snowflake solution extension.

 

Together, this foundation delivers a complete understanding of your business built on knowledge only SAP can provide: business process logic, rich operational data products, intelligent content, and global industry deployments. With AI and Joule Agents, that trusted business context becomes action, helping customers automate processes and make faster, better-informed decisions.

SAP Business Data Cloud is a fully managed SaaS solution that unifies and governs all SAP data and seamlessly connects with third-party data—giving line-of-business leaders context to make even more impactful decisions. It combines all the powerful functionality of SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, and SAP Business Warehouse, plus managed SAP Databricks and Intelligent Applications, including data products for SAP line of business applications.

SAP Databricks is an SAP-managed version of the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform embedded natively within SAP Business Data Cloud. SAP Databricks brings industry-leading AI/ML, data science, and data engineering capabilities together with semantically rich, business-ready data from SAP applications. Leveraging zero-copy Delta Sharing, companies can seamlessly integrate semi-structured and unstructured data from any source with data products from SAP applications into a single, harmonized data model—eliminating complex data movement with seamless access to high-quality, reliable data.

SAP Databricks is embedded natively into SAP Business Data Cloud and users can access the SAP Databricks workspace directly from within SAP Business Data Cloud.

 

Deep bidirectional, zero-copy data integration via Delta Sharing will enable customers to leverage the rich data engineering, data science, and AI/ML tooling of Databricks with the diverse, semantically rich, prepackaged data products from various SAP applications resulting in faster time to value.

SAP Datasphere is where business data users go to connect, integrate, federate, prepare, model, and manage enterprise data with semantics intact. It offers industry-leading analytic modelling, enabling a more agile approach with self-service access to data and self-service modeling in business terms.

 

SAP Databricks is where advanced data users (like data engineers and AI/ML developers) go to integrate all types of data, develop custom AI/ML solutions, execute ad-hoc SQL analytics, and run data engineering workloads—all within a pro-code development environment.

SAP Business Data Cloud provides a trusted data foundation by unifying SAP and third-party data, along with the business processes, policies, and logic that make your data meaningful. Customers get best-of-breed compute for every data and AI workload with engines that adapt to business needs. Together with the domain and industry models in SAP Business AI Platform, SAP Business Data Cloud ensures every agent, application, and decision draws from the universal business context and semantics, while continuously learning from both existing and incoming data.

Master data management is the discipline of creating one trusted master reference (a single version of the truth) for all important business data, such as product data, customer data, asset data, finance data, and more. MDM helps ensure businesses don’t use multiple, potentially inconsistent versions of data in different parts of business, including processes, operations, and analytics and reporting. The three key pillars to effective MDM include: data consolidation, data governance, and data quality management.

The key is to first preserve the value and quality of mission-critical master data, leveraging a solution like SAP Master Data Governance, and then to share access to this data in a decentralized way with a flexible business data fabric, leveraging solutions like SAP Datasphere. This allows you to also join your trusted, governed master data with other SAP data and third-party data to accelerate your ability to derive value and gain insights from that data.

The purpose of master data integration is to distribute master data to enable a harmonized view of master data across all applications. Master data integration allows for end-to-end process integration across the enterprise. Master data integration does not change the quality of master data, but always distributes master data in its current state. Instead, integration provides a distribution layer that gives your line-of-business applications a consistent view of data. Ultimately, a master data integration should increase the effectiveness and reduce the cost and effort of data sharing.

After your move to SAP S/4HANA, many business processes will be familiar to you from your existing ERP system; but you will also be implementing new, more automated processes to match the demands of the digital marketplace. You may find yourself implementing processes for automatic replacement of parts inventory, IoT processes, really the sky's the limit. These processes will rely more heavily on clean and correct master data, and if your master data is not up to the task, you will lose much of the value of SAP S/4HANA. To avoid this, we recommended that you curate your master data early and well before the actual implementation begins. The SAP Master Data Governance application offers in-built integration to SAP’s data model and underlying technologies (for example, SAP Business Workflow), and helps you consolidate and actively govern master data for SAP and third-party applications.

Frequently asked questions

Master data management is the practice of creating and maintaining a consistent, governed view of all business entities across the systems that use them. It is no longer just an ERP topic—master data is the foundation for automation and agentic experiences across your enterprise.

 

Within a business data fabric, master data management is where that context is built. Entity resolution identifies records that describe the same entity and brings them together into a golden record. Governance enforces policy and quality and relationships show how entities connect, producing unified data products in the knowledge core.

AI agents act on your data with no human to catch errors first. An agent may resolve a customer dispute, reprice a product, or evaluate a supplier. When the underlying records are duplicated, conflicting, or stale, every application, analytic, and AI agent built on it inherits the problem and acts on it. AI agents need the same accurate context your best people rely on.

 

Master data management resolves data from every source into one view per entity, governs how that view is created and changed, and carries the relationships between entities—so every agent works from the same current view.

Data unification turns duplicate, inconsistent business entities from many sources into one consistent, and comprehensive view of each entity—matching and merging duplicates, cleansing and enriching values, and capturing relationships and hierarchies. The result goes beyond a golden record. Each view carries the relationships and interactions that give the entity meaning.

 

A data warehouse or lakehouse collects data—it does not resolve it. Nothing decides which records describe the same customer, product, or supplier, so the duplicates, conflicting values, and gaps come with the data.

SAP Reltio and SAP Master Data Governance are complementary. SAP Master Data Governance keeps master data correct at the point of creation in SAP ERP, enforcing policy and leaving a full audit trail. SAP Reltio unifies master data from other SAP applications, non-SAP systems, and third-party data providers—resolving duplicates and maintaining quality across all of them.

 

SAP has long provided trusted business data and context within SAP ERP. Together, these solutions extend that trusted foundation across all your SAP and non-SAP systems.

Mastering data in SAP ERP alone isn’t enough because the entities your business runs on exist in multiple places. For example, a customer exists in ERP, but also in CRM, marketing, commerce, service systems, and often in third-party data. Governing master data at creation keeps ERP correct, but it can’t resolve the duplicates, conflicting values, and missing relationships that appear once the same entity is represented across a dozen other systems.

 

AI agents act on the whole entity—not just the ERP portion of it. Unifying data across sources gives them a comprehensive, current view rather than an authoritative fragment.

SAP Reltio is the data unification and MDM capability of SAP Business Data Cloud. It unifies master data from SAP and non-SAP sources into comprehensive views of customers, products, suppliers, locations, and assets and the relationships, hierarchies, and interactions between them.

 

Those unified views are published as unified data products that operational applications, analytics, and AI agents consume in milliseconds, and they form part of the knowledge core of SAP Business Data Cloud.

SAP Reltio and SAP Master Data Governance are complementary and sit in the same layer of the business data fabric. SAP Master Data Governance enforces governance and process control at the point of data creation in SAP ERP, so master data is correct from the start and fully auditable. SAP Reltio unifies master data across any source—other SAP applications, non-SAP systems, and third-party data—and continuously monitors and improves its quality. Existing SAP Master Data Governance customers can add SAP Reltio when their master data spans systems beyond SAP ERP.

SAP Reltio unifies core business entities from SAP and non-SAP sources across multiple domains at once—customers (organizations, contacts, and consumers), products, suppliers, locations, and assets.

 

It also captures the relationships and hierarchies between them and extracts attributes and interactions from unstructured sources, so entity views reflect more than what structured systems record. More than 1,000 prebuilt connectors and an API-first architecture handle the integration.

Agents need unified master data when they act on entities, resolve a customer issue, reprice a product, or evaluate a supplier. When data about that entity is duplicated, conflicting, or missing its relationships, the agent reasons from the wrong facts and takes the wrong action.

 

Simply bringing together data into one place does not fix this—raw consolidated data still contains duplicates and inconsistencies and carries no business relationships. Unified master data resolves inconsistencies and duplicates to give agents a complete, current, and relationship-aware view they can act on with minimal human correction.

products/artificial-intelligence/ai-unit.body:
AI Units
/content/sapdx/countries/en_us/registration/request-demo.html

Simplify AI consumption with a unified AI currency

This virtual currency system makes it simple to consume SAP Business AI. Instead of purchasing licenses for individual AI features, you can buy AI units in packages and apply them flexibly across solutions such as SAP S/4HANA Cloud, SAP SuccessFactors, and SAP Ariba.

Button 1

Button 2

Benefits

Unify purchasing for Business AI

Simplify access to SAP’s growing portfolio of premium AI features using a single currency, without the need for multiple contracts or licenses.

Use units flexibly across products

Draw from a central pool of AI units and consume the capabilities you need most—whether for finance, HR, procurement, supply chain, customer experience, or other use cases.

Tie consumption to clear business metrics

Track how many AI units will be consumed for each use case thanks to predefined conversion rates per request, user, record or other metric.

Plan and budget AI usage with confidence

Model scenarios in advance with simple annual package purchases and built-in forecasting tools, including an AI unit estimator.

Invest in future innovations

Take advantage of SAP’s expanding Business AI portfolio. Automatically access new premium AI features and related feature packages as they’re released.

Plans and pricing

products/artificial-intelligence/eu-ai-c.description: Use AI securely and compliantly with your choice of models on European cloud infrastructure designed to support GDPR, EU AI Act, and sovereignty requirements.
products/artificial-intelligence/eu-ai-c.body:
Artificial Intelligence
Overview

EU AI cloud: Secure, compliant AI for Europe

Innovate with industry-leading AI from SAP and trusted partners—hosted on GDPR- and EU AI Act−compliant sovereign cloud infrastructure.
Talk to an expert to learn more
Read the press release

What is EU AI Cloud?

EU AI Cloud gives European enterprises and German public sector organizations secure, compliant cloud environments for building and running AI. It provides governed access to auditable LLMs from SAP and trusted partners, while meeting EU AI Act and GDPR regulations and supporting European sovereignty needs.

Advanced AI technologies

Accessed from SAP and trusted partners through a single API, running optimally on high-performance European infrastructure.

Build, deploy, and manage AI on a governed foundation

Built on SAP Cloud Infrastructure and SAP Business Technology Platform.

Your data never leaves Europe

All infrastructure, administration, and support is handled by local SAP teams.

Enterprise-grade governance

Gain full visibility, control, and auditability, with your AI resources running on a reliable foundation of SAP Cloud Infrastructure and SAP BTP.

Confident compliance

Operate compliantly with local laws and regulations, protected by strong contractual safeguards and built-in security. Your data stays private, encrypted, and is never used to train third-party models.

Choice and simplicity

Choose the LLMs and data centers that best meet your needs—and seamlessly switch to different options as your technical or regulatory needs change.

Gain the freedom to innovate with confidence

SAP gives you secure, compliant cloud environments with the flexibility to choose the AI models that best support your business goals—all aligned with EU AI Act and GDPR requirements.

EU AI Cloud

Consume and use AI with confidence through governed, compliant access to leading models—helping you innovate securely, transparently, and at scale across European cloud environments.

Explore partners
SAP Sovereign Cloud

Run AI and core workloads, including ERP, in a sovereign cloud environment that keeps data under your control and meets national sovereignty requirements.

Learn more
The Industrial AI Cloud project

This new initiative from SAP and leading technology partners is designed with sovereign AI capabilities to accelerate innovation and support secure enterprise AI adoption across the DACH region.

Learn more

Featured partners

Cohere Enterprise

Cohere provides advanced retrieval, summarization, and workflow orchestration capabilities, giving enterprises accurate, context-aware AI they can confidently integrate into complex operations.

Read the blog 

Mistral AI

Mistral AI delivers efficient, high-performance models with strong multilingual capabilities, regulatory alignment, and privacy controls for enterprise-grade customization and data sovereignty. Get started today with Mistral on SAP Business AI Platform, enabling versatile, efficient AI in a sovereign environment.

Learn more

products/artificial-intelligence/transla.title: SAP Translation Hub
products/artificial-intelligence/transla.description: Enable multilingual communication at scale with SAP Translation Hub’s AI-powered content reuse and localization features including AI-driven machine translation.
products/artificial-intelligence/transla.body:
SAP Translation Hub
/content/sapdx/countries/en_us/registration/request-demo.html

Streamline multilingual enablement with intelligent data reuse and AI

SAP Translation Hub enables you to efficiently translate custom applications, extensions, documentation, and more into multiple languages. Accelerate translation by combining the reuse of language data with AI-driven machine translation. Use the integrated workflow or APIs to develop integrations.

Button 1

Button 2

Benefits

Reuse and accelerate

Accelerate translations and improve consistency with SAP Translation Hub’s multilingual text repository by reusing verified SAP translations and AI-driven machine translation trained on vast amounts of SAP data. Include your own language data to ensure the right translations for your company.

Simple and efficient

Enable faster and more efficient collaboration in global teams by using one Cloud application that lets your experts (developers, local key users, subject-matter experts) generate, share, review, and edit translations.

Integration out-of-the-box

Integrations with other SAP Cloud and on-premise products mean you can automatically translate your content on demand. Select from a comprehensive range of public APIs to consume automatically generated translations from SAP Translation Hub and Document Translation services in your own applications.

Features

Benefit from SAP's Multilingual Text Repository

Draw on more than 20 years of SAP translation experience by reusing standard SAP translations available in more than 40 languages in the Multilingual Text Repository. Click here to learn more.

Leverage AI-driven machine translation

Use the Document Translation service to translate documents and texts instantly with AI-driven machine translation trained on SAP data. Efficiently translate and review user interface texts with machine translation integrated into SAP Translation Hub’s workflow and editor.

Consume APIs

A range of public APIs lets you consume SAP Translation Hub and Document Translation content directly in your own applications.

Collaborate easily across the globe

Benefit from easy and secure access for global collaboration: Get translations for texts from different repositories; check translations and filter by criteria like the translation provider or quality index; and collaboratively post-edit and review translations.

Integrate your own language data

Integrate multilingual data specific to your company or industry. By integrating your own language data, you can increase the quality of translations and reduce the effort required for post-edit and review.

Translate with a term-aware glossary

Create a glossary with your most important terms to achieve the best possible translations right away and reduce the need for manual corrections.

Plans and pricing
