products/financial-management/global-tra.body:
SAP Global Trade Services
Overview

SAP Global Trade Services

Streamline compliance with new trade dynamics and accelerate cross-border supply chain operations with an integrated platform.
Request a demo

What is SAP Global Trade Services?

SAP Global Trade Services is a solution that automates and streamlines trade compliance processes so you can control costs, reduce the risk of penalties and fines, and clear customs faster.

Centralize global trade management with a single repository for compliance data and benefit from:

  • Comprehensive import and export management
  • Optimized tariff classification
  • Management of free-trade agreements and customs procedures
  • Self-filing and broker communication

Key benefits

Improve efficiency

Handle import/export customs, documentation, and product and tariff classification, and save costs with trade strategies.

Reduce risk

Validate every order against the latest compliance regulations to reduce the risk of fines and penalties.

Optimize operations

Accelerate supply chain processes with real-time compliance checks.

Key features

Sanctioned party list (SPL) screening

Support sanctioned party list screening across sales, finance, HR, procurement, and distribution. If a transaction fails a check, the software blocks it for immediate review. Work lists enable efficient processing of blocked documents, and user-friendly workflows escalate questionable entries.

Customs management

Streamline your customs clearance processes and achieve regulatory compliance by ensuring accurate product categorization for trade documentation and determining the relevant tariff codes for import and export procedures.

Import and export management

Connect with core logistics processes and multiple government customs systems to help ensure compliant and efficient import and export management. Fulfil compliance duties by checking transactions for embargoes, managing licenses, and using inline blocking/release for transactions.

 

Real-time compliance checks and controls

Integrate with order and shipment processes supported by SAP Business Suite applications to keep compliance-related data—and your products—moving as quickly as possible.

Support for special customs procedures

Meet customs requirements, such as foreign trade zones, processing trade in China, bonded warehousing, settlement for inward processing and processing under customs control, Intrastat, and the Excise Movement and Control System (EMCS).

Accelerated application data analysis

Use SAP HANA as the primary database for Global Trade Services. Through in-memory computing technology, the database helps accelerate application data analysis with tools including data modeling, data and lifecycle management, and security.

products/financial-management/multi-bank.body:
SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity
Overview

SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity

Request a demo

Opening the corporate-to-bank relationship with a secure business network

Connect banks and other financial institutions with corporate customers

The SAP Multi-Bank Connectivity solution offers a secure network owned and managed by SAP. You can leverage multiple services over one single channel and support the deployment of new ones.
  • Cloud deployment
  • Native integration with SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA
  • Automated bank integration
  • Support for Swift and EBICS requirements

Key benefits

Connected businesses with financial institutions

Create a multi-bank, digital channel between your ERP system and your banks that offers embedded EBICS and Swift connectivity.

Increased control, efficiency, and transparency

Refine and simplify treasury operations by updating payment status and cash positions automatically in your ERP system.

Higher reliability of your banking network

Automate manual, error-prone steps associated with the execution and reconciliation of payments, order-to-cash applications, and order entry documents.

Key features

Secure multi-bank and multi-corporate connectivity

  • Enable direct integration with payment approval processes

  • Add encryption and digital signatures to messages exchanged with financial institutions

Integration with all financial services providers

  • Embed Swift integration based on a partnership between SAP and Swift

Certified for Swift gpi

Improve your customer experience with faster, safer, and more transparent international payments by using solutions certified for the global, cross-border payments standard.

Take advantage of end-to-end processing within SAP S/4HANA, which is certified by Swift with the corporate–treasury management label.

SAP Price Staging Hub by Vistex is a solution that helps you calculate and update prices in near real time and relieve pricing demand pressures.

Significantly reduce processing times to produce accurate, customer-specific pricing.

Simplicity and versatility

Communicate pricing in near real time across disparate sales channels—all from one place.

Improved customer experience and revenue

Dynamic pricing engine

  • Provide immediate, accurate pricing for sales and quoting applications

High-volume price retrieval

  • Handle increasing transaction volumes via web shops and other sales channels

  • Schedule fast updates of affected pricing to keep repository accurate

Price recalculation and catalog management

  • Calculate prices in near real time to ensure up-to-date pricing

products/financial-management/profitabil.description: See how SAP Profitability and Performance Management enhances financial and operational efficiency with advanced business modeling and real-time insights.
products/financial-management/profitabil.body:
SAP Profitability and Performance Management
Overview

SAP Profitability and Performance Management

Steer a course for optimal performance with direct tax and granular profit and cost analysis to act faster and with more agility.
Request a demo

What is SAP Profitability and Performance Management?

SAP Profitability and Performance Management is an application that offers advanced business modeling of complex processes to help maximize your business performance and profitability.

Empower business users to make more strategic decisions by:

  • Using AI to translate business intents in simple and fast actions.

  • Amplifying insights with multidimensional granular profit and cost analysis.

  • Accelerating corporate income tax calculations and operational transfer pricing.

  • Extending ERP for business-, location-, and regulation-specific needs.

Key benefits

Enabling precision with impactful models

Access advanced modeling capabilities for creating meaningful insights through sophisticated business-centric profitability, cost, and process use case models.

Amplifying and extending your insights

Complement current intelligence to add deeper and richer analysis shaped to your business needs, then extend these new insights across an enterprise of users.

Activating steering through real-time decisions

Act with speed and agility and steer a course toward optimal performance by making informed strategic decisions based on real-time results and simulations.

Simplifying execution of business intents with AI

Achieve business intents through using natural language to coordinate AI agents.

Key features

Advanced business-centric modeling

  • Empower your team to create complex direct tax, cost, and profitability models with intuitive tools.

  • Build business-relevant models by using predefined content and comprehensive allocations.

  • Support trust and confidence by replacing spreadsheets with a flexible, repeatable, and transparent process.

 

Extended insights across the enterprise

  • Add deeper, richer analysis and share valuable new insights with cloud users.

  • Complement established procedures to harmonize results with enterprise processes and reports.

  • Create a single source of truth for direct tax and profitability and performance insights.

Immediate access to actionable insights

  • Make better-informed decisions in the moment with instant insights based on deep granular analysis.

  • Be proactive and decisive and cut cycle times with in-memory calculations that deliver real-time analysis.

  • Inspire confidence in decisions by simulating and reviewing before you act.

Coordinated AI agents with dedicated skill sets

  • Achieve business intents more efficiently through the use of AI agents.

  • Coordinate AI agents with product skill sets such as models, reporting, processes, and simulations.

  • Offer the flexibility and extensibility of business AI agents to coordinate product-skilled AI agents.

SAP Direct Tax Management

  • Manage operational transfer pricing, IFRS tax reporting, and OECD BEPS Pillar 2 in a single solution powered by SAP Profitability and Performance Management Cloud.

  • Enable tax results to automatically feed from one area to another supported by a harmonized data foundation.

  • Coordinate agents to translate business intent into action.

SAP S/4HANA for contract, lease, and real estate mgt.
Overview

SAP S/4HANA for contract, lease, and real estate management

Commercial and corporate management software that streamlines and enhances real estate processes across industries and organizations
Request a demo

Simplifying your residential and commercial real estate processes

Gain a 360-degree view of your real estate portfolio performance

  • Commercial, corporate, and residential process support
  • New lease accounting standards support

Extend your SAP Cloud ERP solution with integrated real estate management tools from SAP partner Planon.

View the product

A single source for contract management

Manage all contracts related to your real estate portfolio in one location, including lease-in, lease-out, customer, and vendor contracts.

Improved sustainability of real estate holdings

Facilitate sustainable property portfolio management that drives greater efficiencies with the help of strategic analytics capabilities.

Businesswide integration of real estate data

Real estate objects management

Intelligent real estate management

  • Integrate SAP S/4HANA for contract, lease, and real estate management with SAP Cloud for Real Estate for SAP Intelligent Real Estate

Revenue management solutions from SAP compose a modular portfolio for lead-to-cash processes, connecting sales, billing, cash collection, and revenue recognition. They support products, services, projects, subscriptions, and usage-based offerings with integrated processes, automation, and visibility across the revenue lifecycle.

Revenue management solutions from SAP support audit-ready, traceable lead-to-cash processes and help align revenue handling with ASC 606 and IFRS 15. They support complex scenarios such as subscriptions, usage-based pricing, and bundled offerings by improving data consistency and coordination across sales and finance, helping reduce manual effort and compliance risk.

Revenue management solutions from SAP support subscription- and usage-based models with flexible packaging and pricing, recurring and usage billing, and scalable processing of high-volume events and charges. They help improve billing accuracy, reduce revenue leakage, and keep revenue recognition aligned through contract changes, invoicing, and cash collection.

Lead-to-cash covers the revenue lifecycle from early customer engagement through price optimization, quoting, contracting, billing, cash collection, and revenue recognition. It spans multiple teams and systems, so consistent data and handoffs are critical. Revenue management solutions from SAP help connect these steps to keep revenue processes accurate, compliant, and scalable as business models evolve.

Margin optimization is the practice of maximizing net margin by taking control of every factor that affects it, from pricing and trade promotions to channel incentives, vendor programs, and royalty management. SAP offers integrated cloud-based solutions that provide comprehensive gross-to-net visibility, enabling price optimization. By governing margin decisions in a unified portfolio, organizations gain the insights and control needed to align pricing and incentive strategies with profitability goals.

Connect asset and service planning, scheduling, dispatch, and execution in one AI-assisted solution to help you:

Increase workforce productivity

Empower technicians

Improve operational coordination

Connect service, maintenance, and execution processes in one solution to reduce handoff friction and keep work moving smoothly.

Key features

Planning, scheduling, and dispatch

Frequently asked questions

SAP Field Service and Asset Management is an AI-enhanced execution solution that brings together planning, scheduling, dispatch, and mobile execution across asset and service operations. It supports both asset-centric and customer service work in one connected environment, helping organizations coordinate resources, guide field teams, and execute work more efficiently with embedded intelligence, automation, mobile-first capabilities, and a more sustainable approach to operations.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management helps organizations manage customer-facing service work from planning through execution. The product supports scheduling and dispatching based on skills, availability, location, and priority, while giving technicians mobile access to job details, guided workflows, and AI-enhanced insights. This helps service teams improve responsiveness, coordinate work more effectively, and complete service tasks with greater consistency.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management supports maintenance planning, scheduling, dispatch, and mobile execution for asset-intensive operations. It helps organizations manage work on critical assets with greater coordination across planners, schedulers, dispatchers, and technicians. By connecting execution with broader asset management processes, the product helps maintenance teams carry out inspections, repairs, and emergency tasks more efficiently in the field.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management extends scheduling and dispatch to contractors and subcontractors alongside your employed workforce. External workers are managed with their own skills, and capacity, and access assigned work through dedicated portals - giving organizations full visibility and control across their entire workforce in a single platform.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management uses AI and automation to support planning, scheduling, dispatch, technician guidance, and execution. Embedded intelligence can help teams optimize assignments, surface recommendations, generate summaries, and streamline workflows across maintenance and customer service operations. By reducing manual effort and improving execution support, the product helps organizations keep work moving efficiently across asset and service processes.

With SAP Field Service and Asset Management, AI handles routine scheduling decisions automatically - matching the right technician to each job based on skills, location, and availability. This frees planners to focus on exceptions rather than manual assignments, resulting in faster response times, higher first-time fix rates, and lower operational cost.

SAP Field Service and Asset Management includes a cloud-native mobile app for technicians at customer sites and on production shopfloors. Technicians receive assignments, access asset history, record time and materials, and close work orders - online or fully offline. The native iOS, Android or Windows app updates automatically with every release, requiring no manual IT intervention.

Yes. SAP Field Service and Asset Management works independently of SAP Cloud ERP and supports other ERP environments. For SAP Cloud ERP customers, native integration automatically synchronizes field activity with ERP financials, supply chain, and asset records in real time - eliminating custom middleware and delivering the full suite value.

/content/sapdx/countries/en_us/registration/request-demo.html

Recommend the best-fitting product or configuration based on end-customer needs

SAP Intelligent Product Recommendation leverages historical data and machine learning to streamline and simplify the quotation process and customer experience for configurable products. Recommend the best products, default configuration options, price estimate, and more based on customer needs.

Benefits

  • Enhance sales through improved product personalization

    Increase revenue with better product personalization Provide solution recommendations with higher relevance, minimize new sales rep training time, expand in new markets, and increase quote to order conversion rates.

  • Reduce time to create a configured quote

    Recommend the best products and configuration options based on the customer’s needs, price estimate, and other elements, such as lead time, total cost of ownership, and weight.

  • Reduce inventory carrying cost

    Leverage machine learning algorithms to analyze historical sales data and market trends to predict future sales more consistently and reduce sales variability.

  • Improve time to full productivity of new hires

    Reduce the time needed for training on complex product configuration, enabling new hires to work productively earlier and relieve veteran employees as well as increase quote output earlier.

Features

View media gallery

Defining end-customer needs and requirements

Leveraging the latest in SAP AI for manufacturers and distributors of complex products, SAP Intelligent Product Recommendation takes a ‘customer needs-centric’ approach instead of ‘technical parameters-centric’ method.

Data-driven intelligent recommendations

SAP Intelligent Product Recommendation works by leveraging historical data and machine learning to streamline and simplify the quotation process for configurable products, enabling you to recommend the best products based on stated customer needs.

Extract customer needs from unstructured text

The AI capability helps more quickly process end-user requirements that come as unstructured text, such as e-mail and Word files. This AI capability analyzes the text and gives the user hints about required product attributes needed by the end user.

SAP Customer Checkout, cloud edition, is a cloud-based POS system for retail, sports and entertainment, and catering businesses. It supports common POS needs, various payment methods, gift card, loyalty, and coupon management, and integrates with SAP S/4HANA Cloud. The solution comprises SAP Customer Checkout manager, cloud edition, which is a centralized platform for seamless POS operations, and SAP Customer Checkout POS, cloud edition, which enhances in-store sales and transaction efficiency. These components ensure integrated POS functionalities and smooth system management.

The cloud edition of SAP Customer Checkout supports the legal requirements in Germany, Switzerland, Austria, United Kingdom, Ireland, and France. The cloud edition can also run in the United States, supporting local tax calculation and offering Avalara integration. However, business cases are unique. It is the responsibility of SAP partners and customers to provide necessary adaptations on a project basis. The cloud edition can be sold in non-localized countries, but SAP partners are responsible for localizing the solution. Also, please note we operate in one data center located in Europe.

The UI of the cloud edition of SAP Customer Checkout (POS system and manager component) is available in the following languages: Arabic (limited support), Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Greek, Hebrew (limited support), Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Portuguese (Portugal), Russian, Simplified Chinese, Slovakian, Spanish, and Swedish.

SAP Asset Information Workbench
Overview

SAP Asset Information Workbench by Prometheus Group

Create a digital replica of your physical assets, processes, and systems to make twinning a reality for your enterprise.
Request a demo
Request a quote

Create a digital twin to help manage your enterprise assets

By making a digital replica of your physical assets, processes, and systems, you can identify potential problems before they occur, prevent downtime, and use simulations to explore new ways to improve efficiency or plan for the future. 

  • On-premise deployment

  • Simplified asset master data governance with a centralized view and reduced time to create complex hierarchical data structures

  • Ability to maintain, revise, and review master data modification for large-scale projects in the staging area

  • Synchronized asset master data and documents in one place

Key Benefits

Access complete, consistent asset master data

Improve your master data governance productivity by making complex multi-object change requests or large-scale master data changes in one simple step.

Reduce the risk of safety and compliance incidents

Provide consistent, synchronized data from all systems of records, accessible from one view, to mitigate environmental and health and safety risks.

Improve plant availability and reduce downtime

Track and monitor your maintenance work with uniform master data, which shrinks downtime and improves shop-floor productivity.

Key Features

Creation and maintenance of complete asset structures

  • Use an advanced user interface for multi-change object requests to efficiently handle a complete asset structure

  • Improve usability with intuitive hierarchy processing, including search, copy, and replace

  • Help ensure consistent relations throughout the hierarchy with functional location structuring, extended inheritance, and cross-object rules

Integration with SAP Asset Intelligence Network

  • Access external and internal sources of information to enrich asset data that can be propagated to internal systems of record

  • Optimize maintenance processes and asset improvement programs by collaborating with OEMs

  • Connect to the cloud-based network for information exchange and collaboration with suppliers, OEMs, and more

Predefined master data model for enterprise assets

  • Create and sustain master data models for reuse, based on prebuilt reference model libraries and best practices

  • Gain relative and contextual views of asset, work, and spare part objects with an intuitive cross-object hierarchy viewer

  • Use extended and flexible workflow processing for mixed objects to quickly adapt to customer business processes

Simplified data maintenance

  • Enhance your workflow inbox with integrated content and fast, integrated processing of workflow tasks

  • Get a quick view of the entire list of master data for enterprise asset management and drill down to a specific data object

  • Use built-in workflows and business rules to help ensure that changes to data are consistent with the predetermined business rules

Featured highlights

Data entry: repost data

Save time in planning with data reposting in SAP Analytics Cloud. Change dimension values on booked member combinations to repost data to unbooked target member combinations directly in your table, without leaving your planning context.

Streamline planning data entry by adding one or five member combinations at once. Paste content from the clipboard, use automatic validation to identify invalid entries, including master data, and correct highlighted values before submitting updates for processing.

Advanced formulas: string manipulation functions

Simplify planning models with string functions in SAP Analytics Cloud advanced formulas. Merge strings with CONCAT, select starting or ending characters with LEFT and RIGHT, and extract substrings with SUBSTR to reduce dependencies and make models easier to understand.

Filter: two new ways to filter tables

Focus your analysis with two new table filters. Apply conditions such as greater than, less than, or equal to a threshold directly in the widget, without model changes. Filter from row or column headers without opening the builder panel.

Sorting in waterfall charts

Explore waterfall charts with sorting in the quick action menu: ascending, descending, custom, highest-to-lowest, or lowest-to-highest. Sort by variance value in variance mode to surface key differences. Waterfall charts also support linked analysis as both sources and targets for cross-widget interactions.

Frequently asked questions

SAP products branded as “SAP Crystal” are on-premise software tools used for data visualization, data analysis, pixel-prefect data reporting as well as data sharing and distribution in various formats.

  • SAP Crystal Reports allows a report designer to include data from various sources to create a document on his/her desktop computer where the data is formatted into a design of their choosing, such as an invoice, a sales or operational report, a marketing letter, or some sort of analytic visualization.

  • SAP Crystal Server provides a platform environment through which you can share documents (such as SAP Crystal Reports files) with end users.

With SAP Crystal Server (user), you can schedule reports to be pushed out to recipients as PDF email attachments, access the reports securely, and refresh the data by entering various parameters.

With SAP Crystal Server (CS – Concurrent Sessions), you can automatically distribute reports customized for individual recipients.

You can as well access reports by using a browser or a mobile app.

  • SAP Crystal Reports for Visual Studio (using.NET) and SAP Crystal Reports for Eclipse (using JAVA) are free add-ons for developers using .NET and Java to embed reporting capabilities into their own applications.

  • SAP Crystal Reports Viewer is a free desktop application (Windows or Mac) allowing recipients of SAP Crystal Reports files (.rpt file extension) to open the document and interact with the data saved within the file, including search, drill-down, print and export – but not refresh (which requires SAP Crystal Reports).

  • SAP Crystal Reports, version for the SAP Business One solution allows users of SAP Business One to create pixel-perfect reports and dashboards by connecting exclusively the SAP Business One data model with the SAP Crystal Reports environment. You can launch SAP Crystal reports and dashboards directly from SAP Business One. If you want to connect to additional data sources including SAP Business One data sources, you will need to acquire SAP Crystal Reports.

  • Note that thrid-party applications from various vendors can leverage a runtime license of SAP Crystal Reports. These are typically sold with the 3rd party application. These cannot be purchased from SAP, but a user can buy the full version of SAP Crystal Reports to also leverage data from outside the thrid-party application.

Start with SAP Crystal Reports to create a report. SAP Crystal Server distributes reports by pushing reports out, for example as a scheduled email attachment. SAP Crystal Server also provides a portal for end users to access content securely via a browser or mobile app to view, enter parameters, refresh, and print or export a report.

People who use SAP Crystal Reports are usually those who use data a lot in their day-to-day roles, such as database administrators, IT, finance, accounting, and power users. The people who log on to the portal provided by SAP Crystal Server to access pre-built content are usually end users, business users, and management – in other words, consumers of reports who want answers to a business question already asked on their behalf (by those who created the report with SAP Crystal Reports).

SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server
Overview

SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server

Support real-time replication of data from SAP or third-party systems to SAP HANA to run applications and analyze data quickly.
Request a meeting

What is SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server?

SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server is part of SAP Business Technology Platform, supporting real-time replication of data from SAP or third-party systems to SAP HANA to help you run applications and analyze data quickly.

Access the right information at the right place in the right time by moving data in real time between different systems within the same network, wide-area networks, and in the cloud. SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server integrates with software such as SAP HANA, SAP S/4HANA for central finance foundation, and SAP BW/4HANA.

  • On-premise deployment
  • Run real-time reporting
  • Use plug-and-play configuration
  • Simplify integration with SAP software

Benefits

Accelerate real-time replication

Enable your implementation of the SAP HANA solution to work with up-to-date information from a productive source system.

Reduce your volume of data

Lower the quantity of data transferred to delta technology with SAP solutions, such as SAP BW/4HANA, which can significantly decrease data loads.

Create a central foundation for real-time finance

Use SAP Landscape Transformation Replication Server as the replication engine for SAP S/4HANA for central finance foundation.

Features

Reduced time and effort of configuration

  • Automate non-Unicode and Unicode conversion during data loading and replication

  • Translate complex SAP application structures immediately into transparent table structures

  • Support cluster, pool, and INDX-like tables

Replication in large, distributed landscapes

  • Replicate data efficiently within large, globally distributed system landscapes

  • Capture change data with near-zero impact to reduce data transfer to target systems

  • Embed the replication server as middleware and deploy it without operational disruption

Realization of transformative capabilities

  • Convert, enrich, and reduce target records

  • Provide extensive data and structure transformation capabilities

  • Offer flexible filtering options to minimize data records from the source table

Enablement of transactional integrity

  • Support point-in-time recovery

  • Integrate with standard high-availability setups

  • Enable extensive logging capabilities

SAP Snowflake
Overview

SAP Snowflake

Extend your data fabric with fully managed data and AI capabilities
Request a demo

What is SAP Snowflake?

SAP Snowflake is an SAP Business Data Cloud extension that provides fully managed, comprehensive data and AI capabilities—giving customers greater choice and flexibility while simplifying their data landscape. 

  • Harmonize SAP and Snowflake data with zero-copy sharing

  • Accelerate intelligent application development 

  • Enable enterprise-ready AI grounded in trusted data

E-BOOK
Extend the value of your data with SAP Snowflake

Explore how SAP Snowflake enables analytics and AI on SAP-managed data products while preserving business context and insight-sharing.

Read the e-book

Key benefits

Build a business data fabric

Provide the right data foundation to harmonize SAP and non-SAP data. 

Deliver adaptive experiences

Build AI-powered intelligent applications grounded in mission critical data. 

Simplify AI governance

Be AI-ready with governed, semantically rich data. 

Key features

Discover and model data with ease

By combining SAP Snowflake data with the industry-leading modeling capabilities in SAP Business Data Cloud, IT and business users can blend and enrich all their data to create a unified view that both users and agents easily understand.

Keep business context intact with zero-copy access

Share data bi-directionally with SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Snowflake, eliminating the costs of data extraction and duplication.

Deploy applications faster

Use the comprehensive data and AI tools across SAP Business Data Cloud and SAP Snowflake to accelerate the development of your applications.

Continuously learn from your data

Build and optimize intelligent applications with a single service that learns from the metadata that flows from your business data fabric.

Ground AI in your enterprise context

Connect your data and metadata in SAP Snowflake with the SAP Business Data Cloud knowledge graph—so business semantics flow both ways, enabling AI to understand your data in the context of its relationships.

Provide users with AI agent flexibility

With SAP Joule and Snowflake Cortex, choose or build the right AI agent for any task—from automating next best actions to building intelligent applications.

Frequently asked questions

SAP Snowflake is an SAP Business Data Cloud extension that provides fully managed, comprehensive data and AI capabilities—giving customers greater choice and flexibility while simplifying their data landscape.

SAP Snowflake supports a range of powerful use cases. Run instant analytics on curated SAP datasets, build enrich-and-return workflows that feed insights back into SAP Business Data Cloud (SAP BDC), and seamlessly bring third-party marketplace data into SAP BDC as governed products.

SAP Snowflake brings together SAP’s context-rich business data with Snowflake’s AI and ML platform, empowering customers to build and deploy AI applications faster. It provides a unified environment where autonomous agents from both platforms collaborate and act on shared insights across supply chain, finance, and customer experience workflows.

Read the announcement to learn more.

products/artificial-intelligence/pricing.description: See Joule AI pricing options tailored for your business needs. Compare plans and harness AI to transform your interactions with SAP seamlessly.
products/artificial-intelligence/pricing.body:
Artificial Intelligence
Overview

SAP AI commercial model and pricing

SAP AI pricing is designed to scale with the value AI delivers—from everyday productivity to automated business processes and outcomes.
Request a quote
Get the AI pricing guide

SAP AI commercial model at a glance

SAP AI commercial model is organized around three tiers, each suited to a different stage of adoption and a different way of creating value.

AVAILABLE WITH EVERY CLOUD SUBSCRIPTION
Base AI

Base AI provides the foundational AI capabilities that come with every SAP cloud subscription. It's available to every user across your organization from day one, with no AI Units or additional paid license required. Joule Work, base provides an integrated experience to orchestrate everyday tasks while embedded AI capabilities are built directly into SAP applications, helping teams work smarter without leaving the tools they use every day.

Explore Base AI
AVAILABLE WITH AI UNITS
Premium AI

Premium AI moves beyond foundational AI capabilities to orchestrate and execute work end-to-end. Joule Work, Agentic Thinking, provides an intent-based, dynamic workspace for complex orchestration across web, desktop, mobile, and in-app experiences. Joule Assistants use deep role and business process context to coordinate Joule Agents, executing tasks and workflows across your organization. Premium AI also includes high-value AI services such as SAP Joule for Consultants, Document AI, Document Grounding, and more. Pricing scales directly with the value generated.

Explore Premium AI
FREE TO DESIGN, PAID AT RUNTIME
Custom-built AI

Custom-built AI gives you the flexibility to create exactly what you need for your business when you need it. Build your own agents, applications, and n8n workflows with Joule Studio, then deploy and scale them across your system landscape with Joule Studio runtime. It’s for organizations looking to differentiate through AI—not simply adopt it. With consumption-based pricing, you pay for actual usage as your custom-built AI runs and delivers value throughout your business.

Explore custom-built AI

Base AI

Base AI is available with every SAP cloud subscription at no additional cost—no AI Units required.  It combines two essential offerings: Joule Work, base, the interactive natural language available across SAP applications, and Embedded AI, purpose-built intelligence delivered directly within SAP solutions.

  • Joule Work, base is the AI solution that enhances the user’s experience across SAP applications through natural language. Users can ask questions, navigate to the right screen, retrieve information, get contextual guidance, and perform everyday actions—all without leaving their workflow.

  • Embedded AI is built directly into SAP applications, delivering insights, recommendations, and intelligent automation within the business processes where you work—without requiring a separate interaction. Availability varies by SAP solution.

Explore Base AI features

Premium AI

Premium AI is built for teams that need AI to do the heavy lifting— complex end-to-end orchestration, multi-turn queries, running agents, automating processes, and executing multi-step tasks across your organization. It’s priced by AI Units, with consumption-based pricing for agentic thinking, agents and high-value AI services and a per-user plan for SAP Joule for Consultants.

Joule Work, Agentic Thinking

Joule Work is the new UI for AI. A dynamic workspace that, based on user intent, surfaces the right insights, automates routine and complex work, and orchestrates AI agents across every business domain. Accessible through web, desktop, mobile, and in app, Joule Work enables Conversations for quick and accurate answers, custom Skills for workflow automation, and Spaces for visualization.

  • Priced on AI Units consumed per action

  • All usage tracked at the action level

  • Two thinking modes

Explore Joule Work 

Joule Agents

Joule Agents are purpose-built AI agents that automate well-defined, multi-step enterprise workflows across your organization. They are accessed through Joule Assistants which use deep role and process context to coordinate agents and execute complex work autonomously, like smart teammates. There is no separate charge for Joule Assistants; pricing is based entirely on the underlying agents they run.

  • Two agent types: Standard and Advanced, priced by AI Units consumed per action

  • All usage tracked at the action level

Learn more about Joule Agents and Joule Assistants  

AI Features

AI Features are individual high-value AI capabilities you can access on demand—such as document processing and content generation. Unlike agents which are priced per action, AI Features consume AI Units per request or per record processed.

View pricing for all AI Features 

SAP Joule for Consultants

SAP Joule for Consultants is priced in AI units per user per month—designed for consultants working in complex, high-value professional services scenarios where AI value is directly tied to individual productivity.

  • Assigned users, adjustable monthly

  • Fixed per-user monthly pricing

  • Automatic access to new features

Explore SAP Joule for Consultants 

Custom-built AI

Custom-built AI gives you the flexibility to create AI tailored to your business needs—designing, building, and running your own agents, applications, and n8n workflows.

FREE

Full authoring environment

A complete authoring environment to build, test, and iterate on agents, applications, and n8n workflows—with AI assisted development available within fair-use guidelines.

Explore the full authoring environment in Joule Studio 

PAID

Production runtime for custom-built agents, apps, and n8n workflows

When custom agents and applications run in production, usage is billed on actual resource consumption—compute, storage, agent memory, workflow execution, and AI tokens—through the SAP BTP Enterprise Agreement (BTPEA), Cloud Platform Enterprise Agreement (CPEA), or PAYG.

Explore Joule Studio Runtime 

Get started

Whether you’re activating AI for the first time or expanding what you already have, here’s where to go next.

Are you ready to get started?

If you are ready to start your journey with SAP AI, click the links below.

Buy AI units

Try SAP AI for free

Contact us if you'd like to try SAP AI for free or need help finding the right SAP AI solution for your organization.

Contact us

Browse AI capabilities in SAP Store

Explore available AI features, agents, and assistants. Filter by product and industry to find the AI capability most relevant for your business.

Browse AI capabilities 

Activate and track AI usage

Activate AI solutions and manage AI Unit consumption and balances in SAP for Me.

Visit SAP for Me 

See what's coming

Explore upcoming AI innovations and planned releases across SAP solutions to help guide your adoption strategy.

Explore the SAP solution road map 

FAQ

AI Units are SAP's single virtual currency for accessing and running Premium AI capabilities across SAP solutions. Purchased annually via SKU 8019164, they sit in one shared pool and can be used flexibly across all Premium AI capabilities.

 

AI Units are consumed only when Premium AI actively performs work—such as multi-agent orchestration, agents executing workflows or documents being indexed. Unused AI Units expire after 12 months. Base AI does not consume AI Units.

SAP for Me is your central hub for activating AI capabilities and tracking AI Unit consumption, balances, and billing in near real time.

Joule Assistants use deep role and business process context to deliver insights and execute complex workflows across an organization. They translate intent into concrete actions by coordinating Joule Agents. Joule Assistants aren't sold or priced separately—all commercial measurement happens at the Joule Agent level.

All agents are categorized as “standard” or “advanced.”  Standard agents are priced at 0.02 AI Units per agent action. Advanced agents are priced at .05 AI Units per agent action.  An agent action is a single step an agent takes to complete a task—such as calling a service, triggering a workflow, or generating a response. A task may require multiple actions depending on complexity. When an agent is not running, no AI Units are consumed.

Yes, Joule Agents can be extended with textual instructions without incremental charges. Agent execution remains monetized on the same per-action basis via AI units: extended standard agents continue to consume 0.02 AI units per action, and extended advanced agents continue to consume 0.05 AI units per action. As additional extensibility scenarios become available, pricing details will be shared accordingly.

Each assigned user is charged 35 AI Units per month, which includes a pooled request allowance of 22,900 requests per user per month. Requests are pooled across all users, so unused capacity offsets higher usage by others. If the total pooled allowance is exceeded, additional requests are billed at 2 AI Units per 1,000 requests. The number of assigned users can be adjusted monthly.

Joule Studio is available to all customers who deployed Joule (via AI Units entitlement or zero-cost Joule Base SKU) and have BTPEA, CPEA, or PAYG.

SAP for Me provides near-real-time visibility into your AI Unit consumption and remaining balance. If you exceed your purchased AI Units, you may continue using Premium AI services, with additional usage charged at the applicable AI Unit rate per the excess use terms of the contract. For details about applicable rates and terms, consult the SAP AI Features Guide and your SAP account executive.

products/artificial-intelligence/what-is.body:
What Is

What is augmented analytics?

Augmented analytics uses AI, machine learning, and natural language processing to democratize data.

Updated on January 26, 2026

How augmented analytics works

Augmented analytics uses artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and natural language processing (NLP) to automate and simplify data analysis. This helps all users—whether technical or not—gain valuable insights more quickly and easily. The process breaks down to these key steps:

  • Query interaction: NLP in analytics allows users to ask questions about their data and get answers in plain language.
  • Data preparation: Augmented analytics AI and ML tools clean, organize, and structure data automatically.
  • Insight generation: The solution delivers automated insights and recommendations based on the structured data.

This approach reduces manual effort, speeds up decision-making, and makes analytics more accessible across the organization.

Benefits of augmented analytics

As organizations face growing pressure to make faster, smarter decisions, augmented analytics offers a powerful way to access the full value of data and stay competitive in a rapidly evolving market. Here’s why augmented analytics is important for fostering greater collaboration, agility, and profitability.

Faster, richer data insights

Data is one of the most powerful assets in today’s economy, but its sheer volume makes it difficult to interpret without advanced tools. Augmented analytics empowers organizations to uncover insights from massive datasets in real time. This helps companies access the full potential of Big Data.

Improved team productivity

Traditional analytics often requires data scientists to manage complex, time-consuming manual tasks. Augmented analytics can reduce this workload dramatically by automating data collection, preparation, cleaning, and analysis. This gives experts more time for high-value tasks, such as interpreting results and driving strategy.

Data democratization

Augmented analytics can open the door for nontechnical users to explore data confidently. With natural language queries, guided recommendations, and ready-made data visualizations, employees at all levels can ask questions, uncover insights, and share findings—no coding or advanced training required.

More confident decision-making

In fast-paced business environments, hesitation and guesswork can slow down progress and increase risk. Augmented analytics delivers automated, data-driven insights that help leaders make decisions with greater speed and accuracy. This enables companies to develop more informed, evidence-based strategies.

Improved forecast accuracy

Forecasting is critical for planning, budgeting, and resource allocation, but traditional methods often fall short in capturing complex patterns. AI and ML tools can help teams detect these trends and predict outcomes with greater precision. Businesses can better anticipate outcomes and plan proactively.

Cost savings

Relying solely on data specialists can create costly bottlenecks in the analytics process. Augmented analytics streamlines workflows by automating routine tasks and enabling more employees to access and interpret data. This lowers operational costs and increases ROI by making analytics more scalable and efficient.

From traditional BI to augmented analytics

Analytics and business intelligence (BI) have come a long way in recent years, shifting from sophisticated tools for data and analytics professionals to ML-enabled analytics that anyone can use. Now, conversational and generative AI are pushing this evolution even further, making analytics more intuitive by allowing users to ask questions and receive instant, tailored insights.

Traditional analytics

  • Driven by IT
  • Limited user autonomy
  • Provides sophisticated tools for data and analytics professionals
  • Focuses on reporting at scale

Self-service analytics

  • Driven by the business
  • Offers more user autonomy
  • Provides user-friendly interfaces
  • Focuses on user-driven insights

Augmented analytics

  • Enabled by AI and ML
  • Offers full user autonomy
  • Employs AI tools and guided processes
  • Focuses on fast, deep, previously hidden insights
  • Includes new capabilities like conversational and generative AI

As organizations compare traditional BI versus augmented analytics, it’s clear that AI- and ML-enabled tools represent the future of analytics, delivering faster, deeper insights than ever before.

Real-world examples of augmented analytics

Diverse business areas can adopt these intelligence-driven tools to uncover deeper insights, automate routine analysis, and respond faster to changing conditions. Below are some practical augmented analytics use cases across key business functions, demonstrating the technology's value in driving smarter, more agile operations.

Augmented analytics in finance

  • Planning and forecasting: AI-enhanced models can improve forecast accuracy for demand, costs, and revenue by identifying patterns in historical and real-time data.
  • Cash flow optimization: Analytics tools can track fluctuations in payment cycles and costs to improve liquidity across the business.
  • Fraud detection: Finance teams can identify suspicious patterns in transactions, claims, or accounting entries—helping prevent fraud and financial losses.
  • Sustainability compliance: Augmented analytics helps streamline ESG data monitoring and reporting to align finance with sustainability requirements.

Augmented analytics in marketing

  • Trend forecasting: AI and ML tools can detect emerging trends and shifts in consumer demand, helping marketers stay ahead of the curve.
  • Customer segmentation: Augmented analytics provides insights into customer behavior to develop more targeted campaigns and tailored journeys across channels.
  • Campaign optimization: Analytics tools examine real-time performance data to automatically adjust marketing campaigns for better ROI.
  • Channel assessments: Marketing teams can use data to evaluate the impact of each marketing channel on customer acquisition and retention.

Augmented analytics in HR

  • Workforce planning: Augmented analytics helps HR teams understand employee demographics, roles, and distribution to support strategic planning.
  • Compensation insights: Automated insights into compensation data help identify disparities and ensure fair pay practices.
  • Skills analysis: AI- and ML-enabled tools evaluate current skill sets and highlight gaps to guide training and development strategies.
  • Employee turnover prediction: HR teams can identify patterns in workforce data to forecast attrition and support proactive retention strategies.

Augmented analytics in supply chain

  • Advanced planning: Augmented analytics harmonizes data insights from across the value chain to enhance demand forecasting and production planning.
  • Logistics optimization: Analytics tools improve transportation planning, warehouse operations, inventory, and order processing by identifying inefficiencies and recommending data-driven improvements.
  • Risk management: AI and ML can help mitigate supply chain risks by simulating risk scenarios, forecasting supplier disruptions, and realigning demand and supply during market shifts.
  • Sustainability tracking: Automated data insights into environmental impacts across the supply chain help support sustainability initiatives and compliance.

Major challenges of implementing augmented analytics

Augmented analytics offers business teams powerful capabilities, but successful implementation may require overcoming some organizational and technical hurdles. Understanding these potential roadblocks will help businesses maximize their data investments.

  • Poor data quality: Inaccurate, incomplete, or inconsistent data can undermine the reliability of automated insights.
  • Unclear data governance: Poor data governance in AI analytics can lead to messy, disconnected datasets that undermine accuracy.
  • Data literacy gaps: Business users may lack the skills to interpret and act on data-driven insights effectively.
  • Ethical use: Companies must use AI-generated insights responsibly, adopting clear policies and oversight to avoid harmful biases.
  • Analytics transparency: Black-box analytical models can make it difficult for teams to understand and verify results, which reduces trust.
  • IT limitations: Legacy systems and resource constraints may hinder the integration and scalability of analytics tools.

By addressing these augmented analytics challenges, organizations can build a strong foundation for AI- and ML-enabled insights.

Best practices for implementing augmented analytics

A strategic, user-centric approach will help organizations extract the full value of augmented analytics. Follow these key augmented analytics best practices to ensure the technology harmonizes with core business values, goals, and processes.

Define clear business goals

Augmented analytics delivers the most value when aligned with specific business objectives. Before making major investments, first determine key business areas that would benefit the most from faster, more comprehensive analytics. Identify any key information bottlenecks and cumbersome processes blocking productivity.

Strengthen data foundation

Augmented analytics relies on high-quality data for accurate insights. Invest in strong data management solutions to ensure clear governance, consistency, and reliability across datasets. Ongoing validation and stewardship also help maintain data integrity as systems expand.

Foster data literacy

Train business users on how to employ analytics tools in their roles. Having basic data literacy skills will help teams input queries and interpret insights effectively. Look for user-friendly solutions that minimize training time and support self-service exploration.

Build a human-in-the-loop approach

While AI excels at identifying patterns, human expertise remains essential for effectively interpreting and applying those insights. Ensure AI- and ML-generated insights are reviewed and validated by experts before acting on any reported results. Choose AI-enabled solutions with transparent workflows to help verify findings.

Start small with pilot programs

Before embarking on broad-scale adoption, start small with a few high-impact use cases. A phased rollout helps teams get accustomed to the technology, troubleshoot issues, and fine-tune improvements. Early wins serve as internal case studies that promote buy-in and enthusiasm.

Monitor performance and adjust

Track and evaluate the performance of these analytics tools to optimize their effectiveness. Check in with teams on how they are using the tools and insights, and whether they could generate more business value. Regular feedback will help refine processes and improve their overall impact.

Uncovering data’s true value with augmented analytics

Augmented analytics promises to reshape how businesses engage with data—making insights faster, smarter, and more accessible than ever before. Business users across all skill levels can uncover trends, make confident decisions, and drive strategic outcomes. By democratizing these data insights, organizations can remain nimble and innovative amid a rapidly shifting marketplace.

FAQ

  • What is augmented intelligence?

    Augmented intelligence is the use of AI and ML tools to enhance strategic decision-making for businesses. The technology is not designed to replace human insight, but to enrich teams’ expertise by providing faster analysis and smarter recommendations.

  • What are conversational analytics?

    These solutions use conversational AI tools such as natural language processing (NLP) and natural language generation (NLG) to interpret and produce human-like text or speech. When integrated into augmented analytics, users can ask questions about their data and receive answers in a conversational manner.

  • What is natural language processing (NLP)?

    NLP is a branch of conversational AI that allows applications to understand written or spoken human language. In augmented analytics, NLP enables users to request data insights conversationally through text or speech, rather than relying on complex technical processes to gather information.

  • What is natural language generation (NLG)?

    NLG is a branch of conversational AI that allows applications to present data findings in written or spoken human language. Augmented analytics tools employ NLG to answer user queries by generating narrative explanations of data insights.

  • What is advanced analytics?

    Advanced analytics is a type of data science that uses sophisticated techniques and tools—including Big Data and predictive analytics—to forecast future events, behaviors, and trends. Augmented analytics extends these capabilities using AI, ML, and NLP tools to automate key data processes and make insights more accessible to all types of users.

SAP Time and Attendance Management by WorkForce Software is a cloud-based workforce management solution that handles employee scheduling, time tracking, and absence management for salaried, hourly, and contingent workers. Yes. This offering requires an existing purchase of SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central. It is not available as a standalone solution. Visit SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central to learn more.

The solution manages salaried, hourly, and contingent workers in a single platform. Employees can record and submit hours by project, department, or work order, and managers can apply different scheduling and compliance rules to each worker type.

products/hcm/what-is-a-talent-management.description: A talent management system is a software solution that helps you manage your employees
products/hcm/what-is-a-talent-management.body:
What Is

What is a talent management system (TMS)?

A talent management system (TMS) is an integrated software platform that supports the entire employee lifecycle, from acquisition through succession planning.

Updated on May 28, 2026

Talent management system overview

A talent management system, or TMS, is an integrated software platform that supports core talent management processes, including recruitment, employee onboarding, performance management, learning and professional development, compensation management, and succession planning. These processes, and the technical capabilities that support them, are typically delivered via software modules. So, businesses can start with what they need and add additional functionality as they grow.

Most importantly, with a TMS, an organization can link human resource planning to its business strategy. This ensures proactive measures are in place to provide the necessary talent that will support the current and future goals of the business.

Talent management definition: the practice of supporting the entire employee lifecycle, from initial candidate acquisition right through to succession planning.

How does a talent management system work?

A TMS integrates all of the HR modules needed to attract, hire, and develop employees. Although it is common for individual modules—such as recruitment or performance management—to be referred to as talent management systems, standalone modules lack the multi-faceted capabilities of a truly integrated system, which supports the entire talent lifecycle and its processes, from initial candidate acquisition right through to succession planning.

Talent management systems typically run in the cloud. A cloud platform provides a range of benefits, including larger data storage capacities, more robust security, and easier integration with complementary applications such as payroll, training programs, career planning, and other systems, as well as the secure storage of employee data (such as personal information, demographics, and compensation).

Modern talent management systems work even better now with the help of AI. By analyzing skills, performance data, learning activity, and career signals in real time, AI helps connect the dots across the entire employee lifecycle. This makes it easier to personalize experiences, surface timely recommendations, and support smarter decisions—so employees get relevant guidance, managers gain clearer insights, and organizations can respond more quickly as talent needs change.

Here are the key talent processes supported by a TMS:

The key elements of a talent management system.

  1. Workforce planning: Ensure talent strategies align with the needs of the business. Work with leadership teams to understand business objectives, then ensure the talent strategy supports these outcomes.
  2. Recruit candidates: Source talent globally, nurture candidates throughout the recruitment process, and leverage the efficiencies of a comprehensive applicant management and tracking system.
  3. Onboard employees: Optimize new hire engagement with a dedicated onboarding portal. Ramp employees quickly with paperless new hire processes. Automate workflows for on, off, and cross-boarding.
  4. Manage employee performance: Help employees manage their goals. Use guided action planning for continuous performance management.
  5. Plan and design compensation models: Reward and recognize strong performers.
  6. Develop and retain employees through learning programs: Provide modern and engaging learner experiences. Schedule learning and carry out compliance training. Develop proactive succession plans and actively develop leaders.

The evolution of talent management systems

In the 1980s and early 1990s, talent management focused predominantly on developing internal talent, leading to an excess of middle-management roles. Through the economic downturn, businesses restructured, and more emphasis was placed on attracting external talent. However, by the late 1990s, organizations found they were hiring and losing experienced people at about the same rate. This led to a new focus on retaining and nurturing existing personnel.

HR processes were incorporated, but without a centralized model, each track was siloed and information was often out-of-date. HR and recruiters had to deal with paper-based and time-consuming workflows with little time to focus on strategic initiatives.

Comprehensive talent management systems were created to integrate all HR talent modules within a single platform. Workflows became automated and digital, creating efficiencies across the organization.

AI and talent management

Now AI is transforming talent management from a set of standalone processes into a more connected, skills‑based experience. Modern systems use AI to continuously understand workforce skills, identify gaps, and match people to opportunities for growth—whether that’s learning, projects, roles, or career paths. Instead of relying on static data or one‑time reviews, organizations can use AI‑driven insights to better align talent decisions with business priorities while delivering more relevant, personalized experiences to employees.

With these advances, talent management systems have become essential tools for organizations across industries. And they are helping businesses address a wide range of evolving workforce challenges, such as:

  • Skills development and workforce agility: Identify skill gaps, anticipate future needs, and support continuous upskilling and reskilling so people can move into new or evolving roles.
  • Personalized growth and internal mobility: Help employees discover learning, projects, and career paths aligned to their skills and aspirations—while retaining critical talent within the organization.
  • Equitable and inclusive talent practices: Use consistent, skills‑based insights to support fair hiring, development, and advancement opportunities across the workforce.
  • Distributed and hybrid workforces: Support engagement, development, and performance regardless of where work happens, with digital experiences that keep employees and managers connected.

Keeping the human in human resources

Explore research on emerging HR archetypes and capabilities needed to thrive alongside AI, urging HR to evolve, upskill, and lead the transformation.

Learn more

Benefits of talent management solutions

From a business perspective, a talent management system provides a range of benefits that include:

  • An integrated and centralized data model for all talent management activities
  • Recruitment strategies that align with the objectives of the business
  • Improved employee onboarding, retention, and development
  • Better engagement between managers and employees, including processes for compensation, reviews, and rewards

Specific user-based benefits include:

  • Recruiters: Better manage end-to-end, using career websites, job postings, applications, candidate screening, and employment offers. Applicants can access and explore career websites, apply for roles of interest, and engage within a dedicated candidate portal for interviews and employment offers.
  • Applicants: Easily find postings through career Web sites, apply for roles of interest, and engage within a dedicated candidate portal for interviews and employment offers.
  • Human resources: Seamlessly coordinate all talent management tasks. Use powerful data analytics to inform business decisions. Generate detailed reports to share statuses and results. Create compensation plans and easily prove compliance with government and industry regulations.
  • Managers: Work collaboratively with recruiters for greater efficiency. Welcome new hires and help them ramp up quickly. Manage compensation across entire teams. Use streamlined processes to help track activities, performance, and ongoing feedback for all assigned employees. Align individual performance goals with business objectives. Use reward and recognition tools to optimize employee engagement.
  • Employees: Easily access information and tasks, including goals, rewards, performance reviews, compensation and benefits information, and learning paths tied to individual career goals. Recognize peers and redeem rewards and other benefits related to exceptional performance and results.

Capabilities of a talent management system

A TMS allows an organization to implement an end-to-end talent strategy that aligns with the objectives and goals of the business. For example:

  • Recruitment: Attract and hire the best candidates who, in turn, become high-performing employees, boosting productivity and improving organizational strength.
  • Development: Build skills and adaptable teams to help drive business performance. Identify and cultivate strong leaders for continuous growth.
  • Retention: Help employees grow in their careers, increasing engagement and retention.

A talent management solution also provides operational efficiencies, using a centralized model for planning, data sharing, and other interactions. Digital workflows replace manual and offline processes for greater efficiencies in the backend, allowing HR personnel to focus on higher-value work.

The activities associated with a TMS generate personal and confidential data, which the system stores in a secure database. Powerful analytics and reporting capabilities help inform strategic planning to ensure that the business achieves its immediate and longer-term talent goals.

With a talent management system, the company can easily plan, measure, and communicate talent results and overall value to the business.

Talent management systems FAQs

  • Who uses a talent management system?

    Almost everyone within an organization will use a talent management system, including recruiters, candidates, human resources personnel, managers, and employees.

  • What business problems does a talent management system resolve?

    A talent management system resolves persistent business problems, such as:

    • Manual, time-consuming workflows for recruiting, onboarding, performance, learning, compensation, and succession activities
    • Lack of continuity across systems with siloed data stores
    • Sub-optimal manager engagement
    • High employee turnover rates
    • Few qualified candidates for open positions
    • Consistent oversight for compliance with corporate and regulatory employment laws

  • What considerations must be undertaken before deploying a talent management system?

    A talent management system must be agile to adapt to rapid shifts in the overall business strategy. Determine in advance how the system will integrate with other applications and within the broader human resources infrastructure. Finally, consider the experience for every stakeholder and ensure the TMS meets the needs of these users.

  • How is a talent management system deployed?

    Today, most talent management systems are deployed in the cloud. This deployment model is more scalable and provides enhanced security, storage, and other capabilities. It also supports a software-as-a-service (SaaS)-based business model, opening up accessibility for small and medium-sized businesses with more moderate operations.

Workforce Management from SAP comprises the activities and processes needed to manage and maintain a productive workforce—including budgeting, scheduling, forecasting, tracking employee time, and complying with regulation.

SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking is our time tracking software for employees, managers, and HR teams. It modernizes time and attendance processes with real-time validations and rule-based calculations that help prevent errors before they affect pay. It covers hourly and remote workforces with digital punch clocks, clock terminal integration, and support for complex round-the-clock and cross-midnight schedules. For managing employee absences, SAP SuccessFactors Employee Central provides absence management across 100+ countries.

SAP Fieldglass is our vendor management system (VMS) for procuring and managing external workers, including contractors, consultants, freelancers, and service providers. It gives organizations real-time visibility into who is working for them, at what cost, and with support for local labor and tax regulations across 180 countries and 21 languages. SAP Fieldglass integrates with both SAP and non-SAP ERP systems, reducing reliance on middleware. Learn more about SAP Fieldglass.

A vendor management system is a cloud-based platform used to procure and manage temporary, contract, or contingent workers. Most VMS applications integrate with other on-premises or cloud-based enterprise HR systems. VMS software helps enterprises gain clear insight into who is working for them, as well as where, why, when, and at which rates.

Contingent workers are individuals hired by a company to do role- or project-based work on its behalf, but not as traditional employees. They can be independent contractors, consultants, freelancers, temps, or other outsourced labor, such as gig workers. These workers can be contracted through suppliers or other talent pools, such as staffing agencies, freelance marketplaces, or a company’s HR or procurement department.

Total workforce management gives you a unified view of your entire workforce, covering permanent employees, contingent workers, and service providers. SAP connects SAP SuccessFactors and SAP Fieldglass to unify HR and procurement data, close skills gaps, and manage compliance across more than 100 countries.

Frequently asked questions

Workforce planning is a strategic process focused on forecasting future talent needs and aligning them with business objectives to ensure the right skills are available at the right time. It emphasizes agility, long-term planning, and the use of analytics and AI to anticipate workforce trends.

 

Workforce management, on the other hand, deals with day-to-day operational tasks such as scheduling, time tracking, and managing current staff. While workforce management ensures efficiency in the present, workforce planning prepares organizations for future challenges and opportunities. 

The workforce planning process typically follows five core steps:

  • Assess demand: Forecast future workforce needs based on business goals and growth plans.

  • Analyze supply: Review current workforce capabilities, demographics, and skills.

  • Identify gaps: Compare projected demand and supply to uncover shortages or surpluses.

  • Develop strategies: Define interventions such as hiring, reskilling, or automation to close gaps.

  • Monitor and adjust: Continuously track progress and refine plans as conditions change.

Common models include:

  • Skills-based models, which focus on capabilities rather than job titles, enable organizations to plan for evolving skill requirements.

  • Scenario-based models, which evaluate multiple future scenarios to understand potential risks, costs, and workforce implications.

  • AI-driven models, which use predictive analytics to dynamically forecast workforce demand and supply, improving accuracy and agility.

Workforce planning tools integrate HR, finance, and business data to create a unified view of workforce needs. Solutions like workforce planning in SAP Enterprise Planning enable real-time collaboration, predictive forecasting, and scenario modeling. This integration helps organizations respond quickly to market changes, optimize costs, and ensure talent readiness to achieve strategic goals.

Buy/bot/borrow refers to three approaches organizations use to close skills gaps:

  • Buy: Hire new talent externally to bring in critical skills.

  • Bot: Automate tasks using AI or robotics to reduce manual work and increase efficiency.

  • Borrow: Use contingent workers or flexible talent models to meet short-term or specialized needs. 

This strategy helps businesses remain agile and cost-effective while adapting to rapid shifts in skill requirements.

AI is transforming workforce planning through agentic capabilities across the entire planning lifecycle. Planning agents create plans and scenarios grounded in business objectives. Monitoring agents continuously track headcount gaps, cost variances, and skill shortages. Recommendation agents provide actionable guidance—proposing whether to hire, reskill, redeploy, or adjust the workforce mix. Together, these agents replace static planning cycles with a continuously informed process that combines AI insight with human judgment.

Frequently asked questions

Enterprise resource planning (ERP) is a software system that helps you to manage and integrate the core parts of your business, supporting automation and processes in finance, human resources, manufacturing, supply chain, services, procurement, and more. Enterprise asset management (EAM) is an important business area within supply chain management and incorporates the management and intelligent maintenance of physical assets owned by a company throughout the entire asset lifecycle.

 

Learn more:

  • What is ERP?

  • What is EAM?

A computerized maintenance management system (CMMS) is a tool to automate maintenance and operations management. It allows asset-intensive industries to focus on driving asset uptime. An EAM system enables asset-intensive industries to manage the lifecycle of physical assets including capital planning, procurement, installation, performance, maintenance, compliance, risk management, and asset disposal.

 

Learn more:

  • What is EAM?

EAM software helps organizations manage the whole lifecycle of physical assets including capital planning, procurement, installation, performance, maintenance, compliance, risk management, and asset disposal.

 

Learn more:

  • What is EAM?

Asset collaboration is the aspect of asset management that brings together various stakeholders in the physical asset lifecycle to collaborate, cooperate, and meet asset management objectives. Where asset management incorporates the management and maintenance of physical assets owned by a company throughout the lifecycle of an asset, asset collaboration involves the sharing of asset data and workflow processes across asset owners, operators, manufacturers, and service providers. Asset collaboration activities span asset definition, commissioning, and maintenance, and help organizations achieve optimal asset management. To learn more, read about asset collaboration on SAP Business Network.

Explore how SAP Digital Manufacturing supports agility, efficiency, and innovation with a cloud-based manufacturing execution system (MES) and embedded AI.

Frequently asked questions

MES stands for manufacturing execution system, a software solution used in manufacturing industries to manage, monitor, and control production processes on the factory floor. It serves as a bridge between enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems and shop floor–control systems to help ensure that production processes are executed efficiently.

In manufacturing, MOM stands for manufacturing operations management. It includes the processes, systems, and software used to manage and optimize manufacturing operations throughout the production lifecycle. MOM covers a broader scope than a manufacturing execution system (MES), integrating aspects of the manufacturing process.

MII stands for manufacturing integration and intelligence. It's a software platform designed to offer real-time data integration, analysis, and reporting across systems in a manufacturing environment. MII connects shop-floor systems with business or operational systems, analyzing data to improve decision making and enhance operational efficiency.

SAP Manufacturing Execution and SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence are being retired, and version 15.5 is the final release. We’ve established a program to help customers transition to SAP Digital Manufacturing; for details, see the SAP Customer Evolution Kit for SAP Digital Manufacturing.

The impact of the cloud on manufacturing is profound, not only in the way that companies execute production but also in the way that IT organizations support operations. Manufacturing companies are using the latest technology, such as AI and contextualized data, to guide operations and ensure reliable productivity. This can be achieved without IT organizations having to maintain multiple systems across locations.
