Quick Sizer is a web-based tool designed to make the sizing of SAP Applications easier and faster. It has been developed by SAP in close cooperation with all platform partners and is free of cost.

With Quick Sizer you can translate business requirements into technical requirements. Simply fill in the online questionnaire, an up-to-date survey that is based on business-oriented figures. The results you obtain can help you select an economically balanced system that matches your company's business goals. This is especially useful for initial budget planning.

There are three flavors of Quick Sizer available. If you are unsure which one to use, please have a look at the description below and this blog post.

Please also have a look at this short video to learn more about the usage of the tool.

 

HANA-based Quick Sizer
Please use this version, if the product that you want to size uses SAP HANA as database, e.g. SAP S/4HANA, SAP BW/4HANA, etc. In addition, the HANA-based Quick Sizer can be used to conduct a sizing for the SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, which is part of RISE with SAP.

HANA-based Cloud Quick Sizer
Please use this version, if the product that you want to size shall run in the Cloud; e.g. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and SAP Datasphere.

Non-HANA-based Classic Quick Sizer
Please use this version, if the product that you want to size shall run on a non-HANA database.

Capacity Planner is a modern web application that enables partners, customers, and consultants to size SAP systems by answering straightforward business questions — no SAP account or technical expertise required.

 

Currently, the tool supports sizing for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, retail. Built on an industry-agnostic platform, Capacity Planner is designed to grow: additional SAP modules will be incorporated in future releases.

 

Access the tool here or visit this link for further information.

You can find in the sizing decision tree more information about the right usage of the different sizing methods and tools. If you want to conduct a HANA sizing and you are not sure which tool to use or which SAP note to apply, it’s highly recommended to have a look at this document.

In addition, please have a look at this blog entry which shows the different methods to size SAP S/4HANA; e.g. you will find more information how to use the HANA-based Cloud Quick Sizer for the S/4HANA public cloud. 

Access Sizing Decision Tree 
Read introductory resources

New sizing trainings for customers and partners

ADM115 and ADM114

You can attend our sizing trainings to learn more about the different sizing methodologies and tools from SAP. The training discusses how to conduct a sizing for SAP S/4HANA. New training dates for the ADM115 (2-days classroom training in Walldorf, Germany) and the ADM114 (1 day virtual training) can be found on the SAP Learning Hub.

Introductory Resources

1 of

Sizing Types

Greenfield Sizing

The term “greenfield sizing” is mostly used in the context of sizing of new applications without or with only little experience with SAP software. It refers to the process of finding out what the main load drivers are and attaching some sizing value to them. Very often, this is done in the early phases of a project where actual business processes and required data volumes are not available in detail. For greenfield sizing, standard tools, such as Quick Sizer and sizing guidelines are used.

Quick Sizer calculates memory, CPU, disk, and I/O resources based on throughput and number of concurrently active users.

Complete the following steps:

 

1. Access the Quick Sizer tool

  • Use the HANA-based version if you want to size an SAP HANA database (e.g. SAP S/4HANA, SAP S/4HANA Cloud private edition), or the HANA-based Cloud version if you want to conduct an S/4HANA Cloud sizing. The non-HANA-based classic version can be used to size a non-SAP HANA database.

2. Create a sizing project

  • Input your customer scenario data into Quick Sizer and it will display the results.

3. Check for sample configurations (HANA-based and non-HANA based classic versions)

  • Find the appropriate hardware configuration(s) on SAP Standard Application Benchmarks or on the Certified and Supported SAP HANA Hardware Directory

  • For the HANA-based Cloud version: Check if the calculated HANA memory for business data matches the number of entered Business Users. More information can be found in this blog post.

4. Provide the project name to your hardware vendor, who will then propose an appropriate hardware configuration (HANA-based and non-HANA-based classic versions)

 

5. If you are unable to find the right sizing for your SAP product in the Quick Sizer tool, consult the sizing guidelines.

Brownfield Sizing

There are different approaches for brownfield sizing, depending on the stage of a solution’s lifecycle. The term brownfield sizing has different meanings. It can be an upgrade-, delta-, re- or migration sizing.

To conduct an upgrade-, delta-, re-sizing you typically measure your current resource consumption (i.e., CPU utilization, table growth, and memory usage) to predict future resource requirements. After analyzing your system, you then add the extra load caused by additional users (re-sizing). If you are conducting a delta sizing, the additional resource requirements for example for S/4HANA embedded analytics can be determined by the Quick Sizer. In that sense, delta sizing is a combination between greenfield and brownfield sizing.

 

Sizing after go-live

Reference this overview about productive sizing, including re-sizing, delta sizing, and upgrade sizing.

More information

 

Migration Sizing from a SAP NetWeaver Source System

There are different approaches available, if you want to migrate an existing SAP NetWeaver system from a traditional database to SAP HANA.

The SAP S/4 HANA sizing report (SAP note 1872170) should be used to estimate the hardware requirement if you plan to migrate your SAP NetWeaver-based ECC system to SAP HANA.

If you want to estimate the hardware requirements of an SAP Business Warehouse system after migration to SAP HANA, you should run the BW sizing report (SAP Note 2296290).

If you want to integrate non-BW systems to SAP Datasphere, you should use the non-BW sizing report (SAP Note 3599138)

More information

Expert Sizing

Typically, in an expert sizing, more profound analyses on the results of a tool-based sizing (Quick Sizer, Sizing Reports, etc.) are performed. There are no standard tools available to conduct expert sizing, but there is a large range of possibilities for such additional analyses. 

Very often, direct communication with a sizing expert is already enough to clarify open questions, usually through a support ticket. In such a case, customer specific conditions that have an impact on sizing but cannot be captured in automated tools can be considered as part of the sizing procedure, and sizing results can be adapted immediately to reflect these conditions.

In case of very complex sizing tasks (e.g. when multiple products / components are involved in a sizing exercise) a detailed exploration of  some core business processes may be required, both on functional and technical level. 

Such a detailed exploration could include the following steps:

  1. Identify the most important queries/apps/scenarios
  2. Identify, how they will be used, e.g. filter criteria, authorizations
  3. Run these queries/apps/scenarios on representative test data (quality of test data and quantity of test data). Ideally, on a recent copy of the production data. 
  4. Measure resource consumption (CPU/memory) and response times
  5. Perform a forecast calculation based on the expected usage of the queries/apps/scenarios

Please refer to this presentation to get more information what expert sizing can include.

At SAP, expert sizing is typically covered by Consulting and / or Support.

about/company/history/1981-1990.html.title: History | 1981 - 1990 | About SAP
about/company/history/1981-1990.html.description: Learn about the history of SAP from 1981-1990.
about/company/history/1981-1990.html.body:
History
Overview

The SAP R/2 era: 1981–1990

SAP R/2 software processed data faster and integrated an enterprise’s business functions, bringing real time to desktop.

1981

Next generation launches

SAP R/2 launches and quickly achieves the same high levels of stability as its predecessor.

Debut

SAP makes its first appearance at the “SYSTEMS” IT trade show in Munich, Germany.

Joint development

SAP works with customers to add a production planning and control module to its portfolio.

1982

10th anniversary

More than 250 companies in Austria, Germany, and Switzerland now deploy SAP software. Having outgrown its office space – again – the company constructs an extension in record time.

 

Revenues increase, workforce grows 

SAP generates DM24 million in revenue and hires its 100th employee. Some 96% of its customers use SAP software to manage their business processes.

1983

Much-needed office space

SAP embarks on a third office extension project to accommodate its constant and growing stream of new recruits.

Key metrics

Employees number 125 by midyear; revenues jump to DM41 million by the end of the year.

Trendsetter

German technology company Heraeus becomes the first customer to install SAP's new module for production planning and control (RM-PPS).

1984

From Switzerland to the world

The Swiss town of Biel becomes home to SAP’s first international subsidiary, SAP (Schweiz AG), and to SAP (International) AG, the hub from which SAP conducts its international business.

Human resources

SAP hires 48 new employees, largely to meet its huge demand for development resources for the new modules RK (cost accounting), PPS (production planning and control), and RP (human resources).

In numbers 

SAP’s 163 employees generate revenues approaching DM48 million.

1985

Tools for the job

SAP's data center is now equipped with four servers: three from IBM and one from Siemens. Employees developing and enhancing the company’s software have access to a total of 64MB of main memory.

International operations

Five employees from Walldorf move to the new office in Switzerland and begin supporting the company's international business. By the end of 1985, more than 250 people work at SAP, and revenues hit DM61 million.

Focus on quality

A quality assurance committee is set up to bolster the stability of SAP software.

1986

In the limelight

SAP – and its software – exhibit at CeBIT, the world’s largest computer trade show, for the first time.

Revenue landmark

SAP hits the DM100 million revenue mark sooner than expected, as the introduction of new financial reporting standards brings in around 100 new orders for its asset accounting software.

Local presence increases

This year sees the opening of SAP’s second international subsidiary, in Austria, and of its first local office, in Ratingen, near Düsseldorf, to serve customers in Germany’s Rhine-Ruhr metropolitan region.

HR software

After three years in the making, SAP’s software for human resources management is released to customers.

Organizational changes

SAP raises its capital stock significantly, to DM5 million – an increase of DM4.5 million. With its workforce at 300, it introduces a new structure of organizational units led by department managers.

1987

Under construction

SAP breaks ground on its new training center in Walldorf. Meanwhile, construction continues at the company’s main offices – now in the fifth phase of expansion.

Growing the customer base

IBM’s latest generation of servers makes SAP’s software available to SME customers. SAP establishes SAP Consulting to support new customers.

More international business

SAP makes its first forays into non-German-speaking markets, setting up subsidiaries in France, the Netherlands, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Two new local offices open: one in Hamburg to support customers in northern Germany; and the second in Munich to serve those in the south of the country. By the end of the year, SAP has more than 500 employees and is generating DM152 million in revenue.

User conference

SAP holds its first software conference in Karlsruhe, Germany, providing a platform for current and potential users to share insight and experiences.

R/3 on the horizon

The drive for standardization in software production and the launch of the IBM Systems Application Architecture (SAA) provide the impetus for SAP to begin developing a new multiplatform-enabled generation of software: SAP R/3.

1988

Transformation, going public

SAP becomes SAP AG, a publicly-traded company. In two increments, it increases its capital stock from DM5 million to DM60 million. In October 1988, it lists on the Frankfurt and Stuttgart exchanges, issuing 1.2 million bearer shares at DM750.

 

Image: SAP's first day at the German Stock Exchange: Hasso Plattner, co-Founder of SAP 

Ongoing expansion

SAP opens subsidiaries in Denmark, Italy, Sweden, and the United States. Entering the U.S. market will prove pivotal to the company’s long-term success.

Training center

Back in Walldorf, the company opens its International Training Center, which also houses a gym for employees – now numbering 940 and generating annual revenue of DM245 million.

Customer milestone

Dow Chemicals becomes SAP’s 1,000th customer. Meanwhile, SAP begins developing RIVA – a billing and administration system for utility companies.

1989

Yet more computing power

SAP’s data center now houses servers from IBM, Siemens, DEC, and Hewlett-Packard, and provides 1,224MB of memory.

Easier to use

SAP launches a new, more user-friendly interface for SAP R/2, and new tools, such as the ABAP/4 programming environment.

International business

SAP (International) AG in Switzerland is now responsible for 12 international subsidiaries, including those in Asia (Singapore), Australia, and Canada. There are 1,400 employees operating in 15 countries and generating close to DM370 million in revenue.

Financial markets

In its first full year on the stock exchange, SAP is named “Company of the Year” by Germany’s manager magazin.

Investing in growth

SAP R/3 begins to take shape. It is designed to run on four UNIX systems from different vendors. SAP is now investing around DM85 million – some 33% of its revenue – in research and development alone.

SAP goes industry

The first SAP industry solution – for utilities – goes live at a pilot customer in Germany.

1990

The next building goes up

Desperately short of office space, SAP invests DM135 million in the construction of a sales and development center, known initially as the “Entwicklungs- und Vertriebszentrum” (EVZ) – and now as “WDF01”. Its 1,700 employees generate revenues in excess of DM500 million.

 

Image: Groundbreaking ceremony: Albert Altenbach (building contractor), Willi Vorfelder (architect), Dietmar Hopp, A. Gruninger (structural engineer, from left)

Research and development

SAP AG increases its capital stock to DM85 million by issuing preferred shares. It plows DM110 million of these additional funds into advancing SAP R/2 and the new SAP R/3 System. Prototypes of the R/3 financial accounting (FI) and materials management (MM) modules are already complete.

M&A

SAP sharpens its focus on SMEs by taking a 50% stake in German software company Steeb and acquiring CAS.

Reunification and expansion

East and West Germany unite; their economies and currencies merge; and SAP expands eastward. Teaming up with Siemens Nixdorf and Robotron, it establishes a joint venture, SRS, in Dresden, and opens a local office in Berlin.

Next: The SAP R/3 era

about/customer-stories/cirque-du-soleil..description: Learn how Cirque du Soleil reimagined its entire business from the big top down by migrating to the cloud with the RISE with SAP solution.
about/customer-stories/cirque-du-soleil..body:
Cirque du Soleil

Cirque du Soleil®: Leaping into the future with SAP Business AI

Watch partnership video
Watch AI video

Explore Cirque du Soleil’s journey with SAP

While audiences discover the extraordinary, Cirque du Soleil and SAP continue to work behind the scenes to run many of its operational processes including travel and expense management, the purchase of goods and services, and running its core financial, operational and HR systems.

38

current shows around the globe.

~4,000

employees worldwide.

25%

faster invoice inquiry responses.

The time-consuming research required to identify the payment status of an invoice and its reason was overwhelming. We were looking for a more efficient way to handle this, and SAP Business AI provided us with a simply stunning answer.
Philippe LalumièreVice President of Information Technology, Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group
The Challenge

Re-imagining international operations

As a global leader in live entertainment, Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group continually pushes the limits of performance and creativity. With 38 shows worldwide and almost 4,000 artists and staff from 80 countries, its operations are highly complex, managing over 70,000 supplier invoices annually. The accounts payable team faced heavy workloads, with about 40% of inquiries coming from vendors seeking invoice updates. The organization needed intelligent technology to track inquiries, translate communications, and provide real-time updates.

 

In other functions across the organization, the ability to quickly pivot, scale, and serve growth objectives has never been more critical. From sourcing bespoke sequins and fabrics for 18,000+ costumes to acquiring props and equipment for global shows, Cirque’s procurement processes were vast and labour-intensive. They required a procurement system with a globally connected network with real-time updates.

 

Another pain point Cirque du Soleil wanted to resolve was manual recordkeeping for more than 4,000 employees from different countries. The goal was to gain further clarity and transparency on expense and travel management for over 7,000 trips per year. It required an innovative solution to digitalize processes and unlock insights for optimal decision making.

Cirque du Soleil RISE to the Cloud with SAP

Learn how Cirque du Soleil has embraced a digital transformation using SAP S/4HANA Cloud to modernize its core operations, scale its global business and become future-proof in an ever-changing industry.

The Solution

Flexing AI capabilities for a quantum leap in business process efficiency

Cirque du Soleil’s move to the cloud with RISE with SAP established a scalable, AI-ready foundation to streamline operations and elevate supplier experiences. Leveraging SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) for innovation, the organization now avails of a modern cloud ERP that seamlessly integrates with AI and machine learning capabilities, paving the way for new intelligent tools such as the AI Innovation Assistant.

 

SAP BTP further enhances Cirque du Soleil’s digital transformation by simplifying data management, standardizing processes, and enabling automation across the organization. It  integrates key solutions like SAP Ariba and SAP Concur while offering the flexibility to build custom applications that adapt to evolving business needs.

 

For their globally dispersed workforce, Cirque du Soleil is moving beyond using SAP SuccessFactors simply to keep employee data. With stronger data integrity and governance, Cirque du Soleil has reduced the risk of errors and is taking advantage of automated processes and information workflows to manage its talented people.

 

With Concur Travel & Expense, Cirque du Soleil can now navigate global compliance, negotiate better rates with suppliers, and simplify expense reporting for its staff and performers as they perform around the world.

 

With SAP Ariba, Cirque du Soleil consolidates all procurement data into a single, collaborative platform enabling smoother coordination with suppliers, improved visibility, and better control over complex logistics such as equipment transport by sea, air, and land. This integration also supports more efficient negotiations and optimized supplier rates.

 

With SAP Concur, our workload is now cut in half. The data flows easily and transparently through the system. We focus more on the control than the process itself. It reduces my level of stress.

With SAP Concur, our workload is now cut in half. The data flows easily and transparently through the system. We focus more on the control than the process itself. It reduces my level of stress.

Chantale Périgny
Accounts Payable Manager
Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group

The Result

Flying high in the cloud to reach the outer limits of imagination

 

By choosing SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition through RISE with SAP, Cirque du Soleil pairs modern functionality and intelligent technology with a creative engine at its core. As a result, Cirque du Soleil is seeing significantly less complexity in its finance operations and in managing tour cost centers. SAP S/4HANA Finance and Controlling handles multi-currency transactions, local tax regulations, payment processing, and financial reporting to manage cost tracking for each show. In the past, the company would have created around 140 cost objects for each tour. With the move to SAP S/4 HANA, the company has reduced this number by almost 80%, creating a unified data model and establishing a consistent reporting structure.

 

With the SAP Business AI–powered Invoice Assistant, Cirque du Soleil transformed its accounts payable operations. Supplier inquiry response times have been cut from 48 hours to just 1 hour for urgent e-mails and reduced manual effort. Generative AI now prioritizes high-importance requests instantly and automates repetitive tasks like retrieving invoice data, drafting replies, and translating messages. As a result, non-urgent inquiries are resolved 25% faster, and the Accounts Payable team’s backlog has dropped by 25%.

 

SAP SuccessFactors provides Cirque du Soleil self-service functionality to its globally touring employees whilst enhancing organizational agility and employee engagement to its entire workforce.

 

With SAP Concur and RISE with SAP as part of its overall intelligent enterprise journey, Cirque du Soleil is achieving operational excellence with a compliant and transparent spend management system at the core of its business processes.

 

SAP Ariba enables Cirque employees to browse and select their preferred supplier, order what they need for shows around the world, and receive it on time. Employees enjoy a procurement system that is 5x faster than the previous one, streamlining their entire source-to-pay process.

 

As Cirque du Soleil continues to innovate and expand its global reach, SAP’s advanced technology will play a pivotal role in streamlining operations, ensuring timely payments, and enhancing supplier relationships.

Cirque du Soleil represents true cloud transformation; using technology and artificial intelligence to run all facets of its operations, including connecting financials, human resources, procurement, and travel with SAP Business Suite. Now, it’s ready for show time.

Guided Buying makes it easy.  The end user selects the preferred supplier, orders what they need and receives it on time.  It is up to 5x faster than our previous system and has a positive financial impact.

Stéphanie LeRoy
Procurement Senior Director
Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group

Mark Cornell President & Chief Executive Officer Cirque du Soleil Entertainment Group
Creating live entertainment at Cirque's scale is, increasingly, a serious technology challenge. Thirty-eight shows, almost 4,000 people from 80 countries, more than 7,000 trips a year; that operation demands a business platform built to keep pace. For more than 25 years, SAP has been that platform for us: the backbone of how we source costumes and props, how we move and pay thousands of touring artists and staff, and how we use AI to identify operational efficiencies. As we build the next chapter of Cirque, we need partners who can grow and innovate with us. SAP is one of them.

about/customer-stories/hyundai-elevator..body:
Hyundai Elevator

Hyundai Elevator: Optimizing the supply chain with a single source of truth

Explore Hyundai Elevator’s journey with SAP

Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd. relies on a wealth of data from across the business to innovate every day. However, important data insights were siloed in a complex landscape of SAP and third-party systems. To take advantage of powerful data insights on demand, Hyundai Elevator implemented SAP Datasphere and other SAP solutions.

Simplification was our goal. We needed to empower our employees with a single point of access to data and analytics. SAP Datasphere and the integrated SAP Analytics Cloud were perfect for our use case.

Jeansu Byun
IT Innovation Manager
Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd.

The Challenge

Breaking down barriers to data-driven decision-making

Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd. is a market leader in elevators, escalators, and moving walkways. The company is at the forefront of innovation, having developed the world’s fastest elevator in 2020. It also offers a wide variety of services spanning the installation and maintenance of its products. To continue innovating as a leader in elevators, the company realized it needed to simplify its data landscape.

 

The data landscape at Hyundai Elevator was deeply complex, with data siloed in different regions and scattered across flat files, external databases, and a mix of SAP and third-party systems. Most of the company’s different departments and regions relied on their own installations of the SAP ERP application and the SAP Supplier Relationship Management application.

 

Without a single source of truth, Hyundai Elevator struggled with unreliable data. Employees didn’t know if the data they relied on for important decision-making was correct or up to date.

 

“We had a lot of discrepancies,” Jeansu Byun, IT innovation manager at Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd., says. “In some cases, only the subsystem had the up-to-date data without it being updated in the ERP.”

 

As a work-around, employees asked other departments to send data as Microsoft Excel attachments through e-mail. Once the data was sent – sometimes from multiple departments – employees had to manually merge and process data before beginning analysis.

 

The laborious request process further cemented departmental data silos. It created error-prone duplicates and delayed new analytics projects. Management also had to contend with data trapped in Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel documents.

 

With critical data locked away, it was impossible to get a real-time data overview, which made decision-making difficult for teams across Hyundai Elevator.

Thanks to SAP Business Technology Platform, our data is centralized and easy to access and analyze to achieve rapid business outcomes.

Jeansu Byun
IT Innovation Manager
Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd.

The Solution

Innovating on insights from across the business

Hyundai Elevator chose the SAP HANA Cloud database to support the  solution. Together, they enable a better data strategy. SAP Datasphere simplified Hyundai Elevator’s data landscape by centralizing data sources to create a single source of truth. The solution connects to SAP and third-party data sources, third-party tools, and applications.

 

Hyundai Elevator connected its external data sources, ERP systems, and supplier relationship management (SRM) systems to create one robust data layer in SAP Datasphere. Now, the company can integrate IoT data from its elevators, manufacturing execution systems, and ERPs from overseas subsidiaries. This way, all data models – spanning multiple data sources – can sit in SAP Datasphere for centralized data access.

 

The company's IT team is now empowered to set up virtual work environments with specific data connections for different departments, including accounting. These spaces provide an isolated environment where business users can model company data or upload and integrate local data, such as CSV files. Meanwhile, business users in the accounting department get self-service access to data. They can also model data themselves using SQL or graphical editors. The business builder feature in SAP Datasphere helps users understand data by representing business entities and relationships with business language.

 

After modeling data in SAP Datasphere, users can switch over to the integrated SAP Analytics Cloud solution to work on visualizations, analysis, and reporting. Hyundai Elevator has built dashboards that provide users with a better understanding of the supply chain – from orders and sales to maintenance. SAP Analytics Cloud offers intuitive visualization features built in, so business users can get insights quickly without needing any prior data analysis experience. They can also use the smart insights feature of the solution to uncover trends and insights with the support of machine learning and AI. For management, SAP Analytics Cloud supports real-time dashboards that provide a comprehensive overview of the business to help make better decisions.

 

Additionally, planning features, such as version management and the value driver tree, help simplify scenario planning with intuitive visualization and easier organization-wide collaboration. 

The Result

Empowering employees with game-changing data insights

Hyundai Elevator’s data silos are now gone, thanks to SAP Datasphere.

 

Business users in the accounting department are empowered with better business insights and quick self-service access to data, so analytics projects can start instantly. Now that SAP Datasphere handles data modeling, projects run faster and no longer bog down the ERP systems.

 

Dashboards in SAP Analytics Cloud support real-time and data-driven decision-making for management and employees in the field. “We have migrated field business reports to SAP Analytics Cloud as our uniform reporting platform,” Byun says. “This migration saves us time as well as improving our data accuracy and consistency.” With the smart features included in SAP Analytics Cloud, Byun continues, “we expect to get more business insights from the data that we may have missed.”

 

A unified foundation for data and analytics from SAP empowers Hyundai Elevator to use this data value formula: an end-to-end strategy that combines data volume, quality, and usage to create data value for organizations. SAP Datasphere allows the company to improve the quality of its data, and SAP Analytics Cloud helps employees put that data to use.

 

Hyundai Elevator achieves agility, business value, and ongoing innovation with SAP Business Technology Platform through integration, data to value, and extensibility of SAP and third-party applications, data, and business processes.

Future Plans

Shaping the future of an industry with intelligent data strategies

Looking forward, Hyundai Elevator will go from 0.5 TB of data currently in SAP Datasphere to 1 TB by the end of the year. The company also plans to take advantage of the in-content network to get quick value from data. Prebuilt business content from SAP includes predefined models to connect and centralize data sources in SAP Datasphere and prebuilt analytics dashboards for SAP Analytics Cloud.

Ready to start your journey? Contact SAP to get started

SAP helps Hyundai Elevator run better

Key business outcomes and benefits

  • Centralized data across a disparate landscape of ERP, SRM, and other core business systems
  • Provided self-service analytics to employees
  • Eliminated highly manual data-sharing processes dependent on e-mail and spreadsheets
  • Created a single source of truth based on data from SAP, third-party, and other applications and systems

Featured solutions and services

  • SAP HANA Cloud serves as the cloud-based data foundation for SAP Business Technology Platform.
  • SAP Datasphere connects data with business context for data-driven decision-making in real time.
  • SAP Analytics Cloud provides a range of powerful analytics capabilities through software as a service.
  • SAP Business Technology Platform brings together data management, analytics, AI, application development, and integration into one, unified environment.

Hyundai Elevator Co. Ltd. develops and manufactures elevators, escalators, and moving walkways that have transformed the industry. The company also offers a wide variety of services that span the installation and maintenance of its products.

SOC 1 reports are prepared in accordance with AT-C section 320, Reporting on an Examination of Controls at a Service Organization Relevant to User Entities’ Internal Control Over Financial Reporting, under Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements (SSAE) No. 18, Attestation Standards: Clarification and Recodification. SOC 1 reports are specifically intended to meet the needs of the entities that use service organizations (user entities) and the CPAs that audit the user entities’ financial statements (user auditors).  Please note that this examination's scope does not include the controls and related control objectives of any subservice organizations. SOC 1 Type 1 report on the fairness of the presentation of management’s description of the service organization’s system and the suitability of the design of controls to achieve the related control objectives as of a specified date, whereas a SOC 1 Type 2 also includes the operating effectiveness of controls to achieve the related control objectives throughout a specified period.

 

SAP Enterprise Cloud Services has prepared SOC 1 Type 2 audit reports by an independent 3rd party accountant. This version of the report covers the audit period July 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025.

 

The use of these reports is restricted to the management of the service organization, user entities, and user auditors. A copy of this report is available for all SAP Enterprise Cloud Services customers who had productive and had financially-relevant systems during the audit period covered by the report.

Finanzdokumente
21. Oktober 2026

Ergebnisse für Q3 2026

Christian Klein, Vorstandsvorsitzender

„Wir hatten ein ausgezeichnetes drittes Quartal. Der Current Cloud Backlog stieg währungsbereinigt um 26 %. Unsere Strategie für das autonome Unternehmen findet nicht nur großen Anklang, sie wird auch umgesetzt. Unsere Kunden investieren in die zugrunde liegende Technologie – von der Cloud und der Datenbasis bis zu unserer Unternehmens-KI. Sie erkennen, dass Joule Work ihre Transformation attraktiver macht als je zuvor.“

Dominik Asam, Finanzvorstand

„Zum ersten Mal hat die SAP in einem Quartal mehr als 10 Mrd. € Umsatzerlöse und mehr als 3 Mrd. € Betriebsergebnis (Non-IFRS) überschritten, ein Beleg für die Stärke und Skalierbarkeit unseres Geschäftsmodells. Mit diszipliniertem Kostenmanagement und anhaltender Wachstumsdynamik in der Cloud beweisen wir, dass wir Umsatz und Ergebnis zugleich steigern können.“

Auf einen Blick

  • Current Cloud Backlog steigt um 28 % auf 24,1 Mrd. € bzw. währungsbereinigt um 26 %.

  • Clouderlöse steigen um 26 % bzw. währungsbereinigt um 25 %.

  • Erlöse für Cloud ERP Suite steigen um 29 % bzw. währungsbereinigt um 28 %.

  • Umsatzerlöse erhöhen sich um 13 % bzw. währungsbereinigt um 12 %.

  • Betriebsergebnis erhöht sich gemäß IFRS um 18 %, gemäß Non-IFRS um 18 % – sowohl nominal als auch währungsbereinigt.

  • SAP aktualisiert ihren Ausblick für Clouderlöse und Cloud- und Softwareerlöse für 2026.

Weitere Informationen
Finanzielle Ergebnisse1

Das Wachstum der Clouderlöse wurde durch mehrere quartalspezifische Effekte positiv beeinflusst, in erster Linie durch eine über mehrere Quartale nachgeholte Umsatzrealisierung von Kunden, die ihre finanziellen Schwierigkeiten überwunden haben.

 

Die Umsatzerlöse im dritten Quartal beinhalteten einen Beitrag von 49 Mio. € aus den Übernahmen von Reltio, Dremio und Prior Labs.

 

Das Betriebsergebnis (IFRS) und das Betriebsergebnis (Non-IFRS) beinhalteten einen negativen Beitrag von 59 Mio. € beziehungsweise 39 Mio. € aus den oben genannten Übernahmen. Auch profitierte das Wachstum des Betriebsergebnisses (IFRS und Non-IFRS) von negativen Effekten aus dem Vorjahr jeweils in Höhe von 0,1 Mrd. € aufgrund einer Änderung in der Rechtsprechung, die einen Rechtsstreit der SAP im Zusammenhang mit sonstigen Steuern beeinflusste, und aufgrund einer personellen Umstrukturierung. Beide Auswirkungen waren im dritten Quartal 2025 erfasst worden.

 

Aktienrückkaufprogramm

Im Januar 2026 hat die SAP ein neues Aktienrückkaufprogramm mit einem Gesamtvolumen von bis zu 10 Mrd. € und einer Laufzeit bis 31. Dezember 2027 angekündigt. Im Rahmen des Programms wurden bis zum 30. September 2026 25.205.983 Aktien zu einem durchschnittlichen Kurs von 164,79 € zurückgekauft, was zu einem Kaufvolumen in Höhe von rund 4,2 Mrd. € führte.

 

[1] Die Ergebnisse für das dritte Quartal 2026 waren auch von anderen Effekten beeinflusst. Weitere Informationen finden Sie in den Angaben auf Seite 21 der Quartalsmitteilung.

Ausblick

Finanzieller Ausblick

Die SAP aktualisiert ihren Ausblick für die Clouderlöse und die Cloud- und Softwareerlöse für 2026 und erwartet nun, dass

  • die Clouderlöse währungsbereinigt am oberen Ende des Ausblicks von 25,8 Mrd. € bis 26,2 Mrd. € liegen werden (2025: 21,02 Mrd. €). Diese Spanne entspricht währungsbereinigt einer Wachstumsrate von 23 % bis 25 %.

  • die Cloud- und Softwareerlöse währungsbereinigt am oberen Ende des Ausblicks von 36,3 Mrd. € bis 36,8 Mrd. € liegen werden (2025: 32,54 Mrd. €). Diese Spanne entspricht währungsbereinigt einer Wachstumsrate von 12 % bis 13 %.

Die SAP erwartet nach wie vor, dass

  • das Betriebsergebnis (Non-IFRS, währungsbereinigt) in einer Spanne zwischen 11,8 Mrd. € und 12,2 Mrd. € liegen wird (2025: 10,42 Mrd. €). Diese Spanne entspricht währungsbereinigt einer Wachstumsrate von 13 % bis 17 %.

  • der Free Cashflow auf Basis aktueller Wechselkurse bei rund 10 Mrd. € liegen wird (2025: 8,24 Mrd. €).

  • die effektive Steuerquote (Non-IFRS) rund 29 % (2025: 30,5 %) beträgt.2

  • sich das währungsbereinigte Wachstum des Current Cloud Backlog leicht abschwächen wird (2025: 25 %).

Darüber hinaus erwartet die SAP:

  • ein währungsbereinigtes Gesamtumsatzwachstum, das 2026 auf einem ähnlichen Niveau wie 2025 (10,6 %) bleibt und sich 2027 beschleunigen wird,

  • ein Wachstum der gesamten operativen Aufwendungen (Non-IFRS) von 80 % bis 90 % des Gesamtumsatzwachstums im Jahr 2027,

  • einen beschleunigten Rückgang der währungsbereinigten Softwaresupporterlöse über die nächsten Jahre, da Kunden zunehmend auf die Cloud umsteigen.

Der Ausblick der SAP für den Current Cloud Backlog für das Gesamtjahr 2026 geht von einem stabilen gesamtwirtschaftlichen Umfeld im vierten Quartal aus.

 

[2] Die effektive Steuerquote (Non-IFRS) ist eine Non-IFRS-Finanzkennzahl und wird nur zu weiteren Informationszwecken dargestellt. Aufgrund der Unsicherheit und möglichen Unbeständigkeit von Gewinnen und Verlusten in Verbindung mit Unternehmensbeteiligungen, die Abstimmungsposten zwischen der effektiven Steuerquote (Non-IFRS) und der effektiven Steuerquote (IFRS) sind, geben wir keinen Ausblick für die effektive Steuerquote (IFRS). Diese Posten können nicht mit vertretbarem Aufwand bereitgestellt werden, könnten sich jedoch erheblich auf unsere zukünftige effektive Steuerquote (IFRS) auswirken.

 

Während der finanzielle Ausblick der SAP für 2026 für die Kennzahlen der Gewinn- und Verlustrechnung ohne Berücksichtigung der Wechselkurse gegeben wird (bei einem durchschnittlichen Wechselkurs von 1,13 USD pro EUR), erwartet die SAP, dass die berichteten Wachstumsraten auf Basis aktueller Wechselkurse durch die Wechselkursschwankungen im Laufe des Jahres, wie in der nachfolgenden Tabelle dargestellt, beeinflusst werden.

Nichtfinanzieller Ausblick

Für das Jahr 2026 erwartet die SAP nach wie vor:

  • einen Wert für die Zufriedenheit unserer Cloudkunden (Cloud CSAT) zwischen 75 % und 76 % (2025: 75 %),

  • einen Mitarbeiterengagement-Index zwischen 74 % und 78 % (2025: 76 %),

  • einen betrieblichen Gesundheitskulturindex (BHCI) zwischen 80 % und 82 % (2025: 81 %),

  • eine stetige Verringerung der CO2-Emissionen entlang der relevanten Wertschöpfungskette (2025: 3,6 Megatonnen).

Business Highlights

Business Highlights

Kunden auf der ganzen Welt haben sich im dritten Quartal weiterhin für „RISE with SAP“ entschieden. Zu diesen Kunden gehören: AstraZeneca, Aydem Enerji, die Banco Bilbao, die Fairstone Bank of Canada, Grupo SBF, Infineon Technologies, Nagel Group Logistics und die NTN Corporation.

 

A5X, Bitzer, BLACKROLL, Greenbrier Maxion (GBMX), die Krannich Solar Group, Petroplus, Rittal und SUZHOU ELE.MFG haben sich für „SAP GROW“ entschieden.

 

Die Österreichische Post, Commerz Real, Decathlon, Fraport, Henkel, MAN INDUSTRIES LIMITED und die Toyota Motor Philippines Corporation haben sich für KI- und Datenlösungen der SAP entschieden.

 

Vertragsabschlüsse über das gesamte SAP-Lösungsportfolio hinweg wurden unter anderem mit folgenden Schlüsselkunden erzielt: Chery Automobile, die DOUGLAS Group, Helvetia Holding, die Kao Corporation, NTT DATA, Tauranga City Council und Wipro.

 

Bertelsmann, Eldorado Brasil, enersuisse, HUGO BOSS, Infineum, Infosys, Mondelez, Panasonic, Roche und Thalia Bücher nahmen im dritten Quartal den Produktivbetrieb mit SAP-Lösungen auf.

 

Die SAP verzeichnete im dritten Quartal bei den Clouderlösen eine besonders starke Entwicklung in den Regionen Asien-Pazifik-Japan (APJ) und Europa, Naher Osten, Afrika (EMEA) und eine solide Entwicklung in der Region Amerika. Brasilien, Frankreich, Deutschland, Italien, Indien, Südkorea und Spanien verbuchten ein ausgezeichnetes Ergebnis, während die Schweiz, Großbritannien und die USA ein besonders starkes Ergebnis erzielten.

 

Am 6. Juli hat die SAP bekanntgegeben, dass sie die Akquisition von Dremio erfolgreich abgeschlossen hat. Dremio ist Anbieter einer offenen, sehr leistungsfähigen Data-Lakehouse-Plattform.

 

Am 17. Juli hat die SAP bekannt gegeben, die Übernahme von Prior Labs, einem Vorreiter auf dem Gebiet Tabular Foundation Models (TFMs), abgeschlossen zu haben.

 

Am 6. Oktober hat die SAP auf der SAP Connect das autonome Unternehmen im Einsatz vorgestellt und dabei gezeigt, wie Joule Work und Joule Assistants in allen Geschäftsbereichen einen Mehrwert bieten.
Außerdem hat die SAP den Abschluss einer Vereinbarung zur Übernahme von TechWolf bekannt gegeben, einem Anbieter einer führenden KI-gestützten Plattform für Work Intelligence.

SAP SE Corporate Governance

SAP SE Supervisory Board

The SAP SE Supervisory Board advises and supervises the Executive Board. The number of members in and the composition of the Supervisory Board are determined by the Articles of Incorporation and the Agreement of the Involvement of the European Employees in SAP SE. SAP's Supervisory Board currently comprises nine members elected by the shareholders at their General Meeting and nine members representing the European employees of the SAP group.

Supervisory Board Committees

The SAP Supervisory Board has appointed committees to prepare its deliberations and implement resolutions – a measure allowed by the law.

The Personnel and Governance Committee is responsible for personnel matters related to the Executive Board and matters concerning the coordination of the Supervisory Board. The Committee carries out the preparatory work necessary for key personnel decisions made by the Supervisory Board concerning the members of the Executive Board, e.g. appointment and remuneration,  as well as conclusion of, amendments to, and termination of Executive Board members’ service contracts and succession planning. The Committee also handles all matters related to corporate governance.

Members:

  • Dr. Friederike Rotsch (Chair)

  • Dr. Pekka Ala-Pietilae

  • Aicha Evans

  • Dr. Rouven Westphal

  • Andreas Hahn

  • Lars Lamadé

  • Nicolas Sabatier

  • Nina Strassner

The Finance and Investment Committee is responsible for matters related to financing, mergers & acquisitions, joint ventures, strategic investments, and divestitures.

Members:

  • Dr. Rouven Westphal (Chair)

  • Michael Gregoire

  • Prof. Dr. Ralf Herbrich

  • Jennifer Li

  • Marielle Ehrmann

  • Dr. Eberhard Schick

The Audit and Compliance Committee handles matters concerning the financial statements and the auditing of the Group accounts. Additionally, the committee handles all investigative compliance related topics as well as the group-wide sustainability strategy of SAP and its implementation.

Members:

  • Jennifer Li (Chair)

  • René Obermann

  • Dr. Friederike Rotsch

  • Dr. Rouven Westphal

The Product and Technology Committee advises the Executive Board with regard to the development and use of technologies and the development of software product strategy. It also covers all go to market related matters.

Members:

  • Aicha Evans (Chair)

  • Michael Gregoire

  • Prof. Dr. Ralf Herbrich

  • Marielle Ehrmann

  • Andreas Hahn

  • César Martin

  • Nicolas Sabatier

 

In accordance with a recommendation in the German Corporate Governance Code, SAP has a Nomination Committee. The purpose of the Nomination Committee is to propose suitable candidates for the Supervisory Board to recommend when the Annual General Meeting of Shareholders elects Supervisory Board members. The membership of the Nomination Committee is drawn entirely from among the shareholder-elected Supervisory Board members.

Members:

  • Dr. Pekka Ala-Pietilae (Chair)

  • Aicha Evans

  • René Obermann

  • Dr. Friederike Rotsch

  • Dr. Rouven Westphal

 

The Government Security Committee is responsible for SAP's corporate activities in context of national security regulations.

Members:

  • Dr. Pekka Ala-Pietilae (Chair)

  • René Obermann

  • Dr. Friederike Rotsch

  • Pascal Demat

Profile of Skills and Expertise

The proper consultation with and supervision of the Executive Board requires specific knowledge, capabilities, and professional experience among the members of the Supervisory Board. To this end, the Supervisory Board of SAP SE adopted a profile of the skills and expertise that the full Supervisory Board must possess. It thus follows the respective recommendation of the German Corporate Governance Code.

Investor Resources

Acquistions
YearCompany
2026

Prior Labs
In May 2026, SAP announced its intention to acquire Prior Labs, a pioneer of tabular foundation models (TFMs), to accelerate SAP’s success in TFMs that started with SAP-RPT-1, and bringing one of the world’s leading TFM research teams into the SAP family.

Date: May 2026
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

Dremio
In May 2026, SAP announced its intention to acquire Dremio, an open, high-performance data lakehouse platform built to accelerate agentic AI and expand SAP Business Data Cloud’s ability to combine SAP and non-SAP data to more effectively run analytical and AI workloads in real time.

Date: May 2026
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

Reltio
In March 2026, SAP announced its intention to acquire Reltio, a leading master data management (MDM) software provider, to help customers make their SAP and non-SAP enterprise data AI-ready.

Date: March 2026
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2025

SmartRecruiters
In August 2025, SAP announced its intention to acquire SmartRecruiters, a leading talent acquisition (TA) software provider. SmartRecruiters’ deep expertise in high-volume recruiting, recruitment automation and AI-enabled candidate experience and engagement are considered an ideal addition to the SAP SuccessFactors human capital management (HCM) suite. 

Date: August 2025 
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2024

WalkMe
In June 2024, SAP announced its intention to acquire WalkMe, a leader in digital adoption platforms (DAPs). WalkMe’s solutions help organizations navigate constant technology change by providing users with advanced guidance and automation features that enable them to execute workflows seamlessly across any number of applications. WalkMe helps organizations reach better adoption of the underlying application, helps companies drive value realization and increase productivity. WalkMe’s DAP works on top of an organization’s application landscape, detects where people encounter friction and provides the tailored support and automation they need to complete the job to be done, in the flow of work, across any application. 
As applications, processes, data and people are the four key elements of a successful business transformation, the acquisition of WalkMe is an important addition to SAP’s business transformation portfolio. WalkMe will continue to fully support non-SAP applications.

Date: June 2024
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2023

LeanIX
In September 2023, SAP announced its intention to acquire LeanIX. LeanIX is a market leader for enterprise architecture management (EAM), driving the modernization of IT landscapes and continuous business transformation. Its software-as-a-service solutions enables organizations to visualize, assess and manage the transition towards their target IT architecture. With the intended acquisition, SAP is building a comprehensive transformation suite to help customers navigate change more easily and permanently improve their business processes. The combined offering will provide a comprehensive foundation for AI-enabled process optimization. 
Date: September 2023
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

SAP Sells its Stake in Qualtrics
Silver Lake Management, the global leader in technology investing, and its co-investors along with the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB), has acquired all the issued and outstanding shares of Qualtrics, including all shares owned by SAP, at a purchase price of US$18.15 in cash per share. SAP will remain a close go-to-market and technology partner to Qualtrics, servicing joint customers and continuing to contribute to their success.
Date: June 2023. See also: Acquisition of Qualtrics (2018)
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2022

Taulia
Taulia is a leading provider of working capital management solutions and offers early payments through supply chain finance, dynamic discounting and accounts receivable finance. With the acquisition, SAP can give companies better access to liquidity and improve their cash flows. Taulia further expands SAP’s Business Network and strengthens SAP’s solutions for the CFO office. Taulia will operate as an independent company with its own brand in the SAP Group.
Date: January 2022
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2021

AppGyver
AppGyver is a pioneer in no-code development platforms that enable users with no coding skills to build applications for Web and mobile uses. With the acquisition, SAP is better able to help customers and partners adapt their IT systems efficiently to their specific needs and optimize the usability of their applications.
Date: February 2021
Press Release (Signing)

Signavio
Signavio is a leader in the enterprise business process intelligence and process management space. Signavio’s integrated cloud-native process management suite complements existing business process intelligence software from SAP. With the addition of Signavio, SAP can now provide a holistic suite of flexible process transformation solutions for customers to understand, improve, transform and manage their business processes at scale.
Date: January 2021
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2020

Emarsys
Emarsys is a leading omnichannel customer engagement platform provider. Their solutions enable highly personalized 1:1 interactions between companies and customers. Emarsys strengthens SAP’s Customer Experience offerings: Their modern, cloud-native, SaaS platform with embedded AI-based automation and analytics capabilities help retailers offer personalized marketing across email, mobile, social, sms, websites and other communications channels.
Date: October 2020
Press Release (Signing)
Press Release (Closing)

2018

Contextor
Contextor is a European leader in the design and integration of robotic process automation (RPA). The company RPA relieves business software users from repetitive tasks and enables both attended and unattended RPA within and across applications. To date, Contextor’s customers have deployed more than 100,000 bots which automate business processes.
Date: November 2018

Qualtrics
Qualtrics is a technology platform that organizations use to collect, manage, and act on experience data, also called X-data™. The Qualtrics XM Platform™ is a system of action, used by teams, departments, and entire organizations to manage the four core experiences of business—customer, product, employee and brand—on one platform. Over 9,000 enterprises worldwide, including more than 75 percent of the Fortune 100 and 99 of the top 100 U.S. business schools, rely on Qualtrics to consistently build products that people appreciate, create more loyal customers, develop a desirable employee culture, and build strong brands. 
Date: November 2018. Purchase Price: US$8 billion

Coresystems
Coresystems is a pioneer in crowd service and a leading field service management platform. The Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered platform provides advanced scheduling of field service activities in real time, and mobile apps that enable field service technicians to perform installation, maintenance and repair tasks. With its unique crowd-sourcing capabilities, service organizations can build and expand service networks beyond their own workforce.
Date: June 2018.

Callidus Software
CallidusCloud is a global leader in cloud-based Lead to Money (Quote-to-Cash) solutions. The company develops software that enables organizations to identify the right leads, ensure proper territory and quota distribution, enable sales forces, automate configure-price-quote and streamline sales compensation. With the acquisition of CallidusCloud, SAP is well positioned to continue meeting the needs of modern sales teams as they evolve – well beyond core sales force automation. The acquisition of CallidusCloud marks a decisive step in the SAP Customer Experience vision to deliver an integrated and unique enterprise sales platform that seamlessly connects the front and back offices.
Date: January 2018. Purchase Price: US$2.4 billion

Recast.AI
Recast.AI provides a rich machine learning-based environment that improves conversational capabilities of SAP’s products. Its technology, supporting over 20 languages, analyzes sentences and returns precise, actionable data. Moreover, its collaborative, end-to-end platform allows software engineers to build bots, to connect them to many different channels and to train their understanding. The chatbots are designed to help, for instance, consumers to procure services and products in a personalized, natural way or to automate service processes for companies, e.g. telecommunications, banks, insurances, or energy providers. Recast.AI’s technology and capabilities are going to be used by both SAP’s digital assistant SAP CoPilot and chatbots across all SAP product segments.
Date: January 2018.

2017

Gigya
Gigya is a market leader for customer identity and access management. Gigya’s customer identity and access management platform helps companies build digital relationships with their customers. It allows companies to manage customers’ profiles, preferences, opt-ins, and consent settings, with customers maintaining control of their data at all times. Gigya’s technology provides new capabilities to consumers across channels and touch points, builds rich intelligent profiles, and creates a consent-based approach to personalization across sales, service, and marketing. Gigya, an SAP Hybris partner since 2013, has customers already using a solution extension from SAP Hybris and Gigya. This acquisition enables the teams to further build upon this existing strong relationship.
Date: September 2017.

2016

Abakus
Abakus provides a cloud-based solution for cross-channel marketing measurement and optimization. The application integrates marketing and customer data, organizes it, and measures incremental value. This enables marketers to more efficiently acquire customers and effectively retain them, and to increase marketing ROI through closed-loop integration with their execution platforms. The combination of Abakus’ marketing and performance management solutions with the SAP Hybris Marketing Cloud solution, including customer profiling and responsive journey management, will allow marketers to understand customer interactions across channels and increase marketing efficiency.
Date: December 2016.

Hipmunk
Hipmunk is a leader in travel search innovation. The company was the first to create a website and mobile app that sorts travel results not just by price, but also key factors important to business travelers such as duration, stops, and hotel location. Additionally, its calendar integration and hotel map search allow business travelers to easily see the best hotel and flight options based on meeting time and location. Hipmunk is also a leading developer of artificial intelligence-powered travel search and travel bots. The Hipmunk team and their innovations further Concur’s strategy to deliver consumer-grade products to corporate customers.
Date: September 2016.

Altiscale
Altiscale provides a high-performance, scalable Big Data-as-a-Service (BDaaS) solution which includes full operational services. Altiscale’s BDaaS is based on Hadoop and Spark, which enables SAP and our customers to make use of big data across technologies, data platforms, and applications.
Date: September 2016.

Plat.One
PLAT.ONE's IoT platform enables the rapid development and scalable management of enterprise Internet of Things (IoT) environments, including connected products, smart cities, connected transport, and smart manufacturing. PLAT.ONE helps SAP broaden its IoT platform offering that includes device management, data management, as well as IoT application and analytics development tools.
Date: September 2016.

Fedem
Fedem specializes in advanced engineering analysis and building software for dynamic simulation and lifetime calculation of structures and mechanical systems under load. With this acquisition SAP plans to build an IoT solution in which a digital twin continuously represents the state of operating assets through feeds from sensors. It allows a “digital inspection” replacing the need for physical inspection. The solution is intended to consider complex forces in play and detect both instantaneous consequences of one-off events and long-term effects of cyclic loads. This facilitates accurate monitoring of maintenance requirements and remaining-life prediction for assets.
Date: June 2016.

Roambi
Roambi offers a mobile-centric analytics and data visualization solution. It enables people from frontline staff and consumers to managers and executives to view, interact with, and share dataindependent of time and place. With the acquisition of the Roambi suite of solutions and related key assets, SAP intends to bring mobile access to analytics to its customers.
Date: February 2016.

2015

Multiposting
Multiposting is a French Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) recruiting software startup that provides automatic posting capabilities for job ads across thousands of job boards. Their solution complements SAP’s recruiting management and recruiting marketing applications by offering a competitive differentiator. The acquisition demonstrates SAP’s commitment to delivering a comprehensive, innovative, and global recruiting platform.
Date: October 2015.

2014

Concur
Concur is the world’s leading provider of integrated travel and expense management services and solutions. Concur’s cloud-based solutions enable employees to comfortably handle their expenses and grant total transparency into spending, helping organizations of all industries and locations simplify their spend management. Through Concur’s open platform, the entire travel and expense ecosystem of customers, suppliers, and developers can access and extend Concur’s T&E cloud. Concur’s systems adapt to individual employee preferences and scale to meet the needs of companies from small to large.
Date: September 2014. Purchase Price: US$8.3 billion.

SeeWhy
SeeWhy is a provider of cloud-based behavioral marketing software that helps convert online traffic into sales and therefore increases retailers’ e-commerce revenues. SeeWhy applications trigger personalized marketing campaigns using email and ad delivery across desktop, mobile, and social channels. SeeWhy provides a key asset in building out the next generation customer engagement and omni-channel commerce platform.
Date: May 2014.

Fieldglass
Fieldglass is a provider for procuring and managing contingent labor and services. The company offers a cloud-based vendor management platform and solution that meets the growing demand among employers to manage flexible workforces, which need to be quickly engaged and on-boarded to support rapidly changing business and customer needs. The acquisition uniquely positions SAP to deliver a platform for businesses to manage their entire workforce — both temporary and permanent staff — from initial recruiting and on-boarding to ongoing development, performance management, retention and retirement.
Date: March 2014.

2013

KXEN
KXEN is a cloud-based provider of predictive analytics technology. Its products automate modeling and analytical tasks, which allows faster deployment and adoption by line-of-business users. KXEN’s approach and product offerings extend predictive analytics at SAP to a larger audience of business users and analysts. 
Date: September 2013. 

hybris
Hybris is the only omni-channel commerce software that seamlessly integrates all selling channels and solutions into a single platform. It provides companies with a single view of all their retail channels and customers with a seamless experience across all these channels. Hybris’ technology helps businesses across multiple countries sell more goods, services, and digital content through every touch point, channel, and device. Hybris enables SAP to accelerate the end-to-end core CRM with e-commerce as an anchor for sales, service and marketing, and a central pillar of customer experience management.
Date: June 2013.

Camilion
Camilion offers insurance product development, product life-cycle, and underwriting solutions that help insurance companies significantly improve the quality of the business they write and bring new products to market faster. Camilion enables SAP to become a leading player in the global insurance market as their solutions cover the gaps in SAP’s insurance portfolio for the US market.
Date: March 2013.

SmartOps
SmartOps is a provider of inventory and service-level optimization software solutions. The company provides key operating parameters and targets for supply chain management (SCM) planning. Their solutions coordinate capacity, inventory, demand, lead time, and product availability variables that enable customers to optimize inventory and service levels, freeing up working capital for innovation and growth. SAP delivers a real time, demand-driven supply chain by integrating SmartOps’ inventory optimization with HANA and SAP SCM. 
Date: February 2013.

Ticket-Web
Ticket-Web is a specialist in online ticketing for sports and entertainment venues. The company provides ticketing solutions and niche customer relationship management software (CRM) for sports and entertainment promoters. That includes a solution for the core process of ticket sales, which further supports SAP’s Sports & Entertainment offering. 
Date: January 2013.

2012

Ariba
Ariba is the leading cloud-based business commerce network and sells collaborative commerce applications used primarily in business-to-business environments. Ariba's spend management solutions help companies manage corporate spending and supply chains more efficiently. Ariba also provides an open business network focusing on supplier management. This inter-enterprise business network creates additional value by optimizing business processes between companies.
Date: May 2012. Purchase Price: US$4.3 billion.

Syclo
Syclo is a mobile enterprise application platform (MEAP) and software provider of enterprise mobile applications. Syclo offers mobile apps including a mature set of applications in areas like enterprise asset management (EAM), field services, inventory management and approvals/workflow. Syclo provides SAP with proven, heavyweight business-to-employee mobile apps for key vertical markets and helps bolster SAP’s overall mobile expertise.
Date: April 2012.

Datango
Datango is a provider of workforce performance support software. The last version of the software and the name right were sold in 2016.
Date: January 2012.

2011

SuccessFactors
SuccessFactors is the market-leading provider of cloud-based human capital management (HCM) solutions. SuccessFactors offers tools for managing employee performance, including performance management, goal-setting, compensation planning, and training. SuccessFactors’ applications are designed for businesses of all sizes, and offer easily adopted solutions for customers of other SAP solutions. SuccessFactors’ cloud expertise and know how, rapid cloud innovation, and proven success running large scale cloud deployments, helps SAP customers more rapidly adopt cloud applications.
Date: December 2011. Purchase Price: US$ 3.4 billion.

Crossgate
Crossgate is a provider of hosted business-to-business (B2B) integration services and a B2B electronic data exchange service that allows trading partners to securely transmit critical business information, including production orders, specifications and invoices. SAP’s acquisition of Crossgate builds on the strong partnership between the two companies.
Date: September 2011.

Right Hemisphere
Right Hemisphere is a provider of 3D visual enterprise solutions. The company produces software which allows users to create 3D models of product designs and manufacturing processes. Right Hemisphere’s technologies enable visual navigation and interrogation of an entire product or asset and all its associated data in a unified environment. The addition of visualization capabilities to SAP’s core product offerings helps customers across diverse industries accelerate time-to-market, increase people and asset productivity, and improve information quality and processes across all lines of businesses.
Date: September 2011.

SECUDE
SECUDE provides security and identity and access management software, as well as relevant assets including development and consulting resources. SECUDE software gives SAP’s applications secure login and enterprise single sign-on (SSO) capabilities.
Date: January 2011.

2010

cundus
Cundus is one of the leading consultancies in the German, European and American markets for Business Intelligence (BI), Corporate Performance Management (CPM), business reporting, and the financial reporting coding language XBRL. SAP takes over disclosure management solutions from cundus AG, comprising cundus Financial Statement Factory and cundus informationCollector, including intellectual property, customer contracts, and a part of the employees.
Date: December 2010.

Sybase
Sybase is an industry leader in delivering enterprise and mobile software to manage, analyze and mobilize information. The company is recognized globally as a performance leader, proven in the most data-intensive industries and across all major systems, networks and devices. Sybase’s information management, analytics and enterprise mobility solutions have powered the world’s most mission-critical systems in financial services, telecommunications, manufacturing and government.
Date: May 2010. Purchase Price: US$ 5.8 billion.

TechniData
TechniData is a provider of product safety and environment, health and safety (EHS) solutions and supplies systems integration, managed EHS services, regulatory content and software to help companies comply with regulatory challenges in these areas. At the time of the acquisition, TechniData had been an SAP partner for more than 15 years, and has helped shape SAP’s sustainability offerings in the EHS arena. Through this acquisition, SAP expands its sustainability product portfolio as well as its market and thought leadership in sustainability.
Date: April 2010.

2009

SAF Simulation Analytics
SAF is a global leader for ordering, forecasting and replenishment software in the retail and wholesale industries. SAF employs the innovative conceptual demand chain management approach, which allows the process chain to be controlled and optimized by its central driving force - the customer's buying behavior.
Date: July 2009.

SOALogix
SOALogix provides standard software packages that integrate project management desktop tools and industry specific project management solutions with SAP Portfolio and Project Management.

Highdeal
Highdeal is a provider of pricing, rating, and charging software for the telecommunications, online services, media and transportation & logistics industries. With the acquisition of Highdeal SAP intends to provide customers a packaged consume-to-cash business process platform to support high-volume billing and enable a reduction in cost of ownership.
Date: May 2009.

Clear Standards
Clear Standards provides enterprise carbon dioxide emission management, helping companies measure, mitigate, and monetize greenhouse gas emissions and other environmental impacts across their business operations.
Date: May 2009.

SkyData
SkyData’s mobile solution makes information from CRM on-demand solutions accessible on mobile devices by linking and assimilating person, peer, and company information.
Date: May 2009. 

Coghead
Coghead’s Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) enables developers, as well as business users without development expertise, to build custom applications rapidly without writing a single line of code or investing heavily in hardware infrastructure. Coghead's PaaS also enables customers to create powerful custom web-based apps and sell them through a solution provider program.
Date: February 2009.

2008

Visiprise
Visiprise is a provider of manufacturing execution software solutions, which help companies of all sizes plan, define, control, execute and analyze manufacturing operations in a single environment. Visiprise’s software is distinctly geared towards specific discrete manufacturing verticals. SAP invested in a minority stake.
Date: November 2008.

2007

Business Objects
Business Objects is an enterprise software company specializing in business intelligence (BI) software. Business Objects enables companies of all sizes to make business decisions based on intelligent, accurate, and timely information. Their flagship product is BusinessObjects XI, with components that provide performance management, planning, reporting, analysis, and enterprise information management.
Date: October 2007. Purchase Price: €4.8 billion.

Yasu Technologies
Yasu Technologies is a provider of business rules and business process management systems. Yasu Technologies solutions enable customers to centrally manage and monitor how business decision logic is formulated and maintained throughout their enterprise applications in a cost-effective manner.
Date: October 2007.

Silk Europe
Silk Europe is an OutlookSoft exclusive regional reseller.

MaXware
MaXware is a provider of identity management software. The company delivers user provisioning, a virtual directory, data synchronization, and related identity management solutions. The acquisition of MaXware is continuing evidence of SAP’s strategy to use well-placed, tuck-in acquisitions to complement its broad solution offering by gaining innovative technologies.
Date: May 2007.

Wicom Communications
Wicom Communications is a leading European provider of all-IP contact center and enterprise communications software. Their solution replaces all traditional telephone systems, offering the functions of a private branch exchange (PBX), mobile PBX, and contact center as a single centrally managed system. Wicom software ensures the availability of services and personnel regardless of time, location, and contact channel.
Date: May 2007.

OutlookSoft
OutlookSoft is a provider of Enterprise Performance Management software, which unites integrated planning, budgeting, forecasting and consolidation functionality. The company is focused on modernizing solutions for Chief Financial Officers, leveraging Web 2.0 technologies to enable collaboration across the enterprise and delivering real-time, predictive analytics capabilities and finance-ready business process flows. Their products also feature an extensible library of procedures guiding business users through all performance management activities and facilitating collaboration.
Date: May 2007.

Pilot Software
Pilot Software is a provider of strategy management software. Pilot Software's application, Pilotworks, provides analytic tools for executives to manage goals and initiatives more effectively and bring structure and consistency to regularly scheduled operational review processes.
February 2007.

2006

Factory Logic
Factory Logic provides Advanced Planning and Scheduling (APS) software.
Date: December 2006.

Praxis Software
Praxis Software is a provider of e-commerce and web-based CRM software. The e-commerce offering is aimed at small to midsize enterprises (SMEs) wanting to engage in online selling and marketing, while NetPoint Focus is an Internet-based CRM software.
Date: July 2006.

Frictionless Commerce
Frictionless Commerce is a provider of on-demand supplier relationship management software. Frictionless Commerce specializes in serving large- and mid-sized enterprises in markets such as banking, consumer products, discrete manufacturing, insurance, life sciences, professional services, telecommunications, and utilities.
Date: May 2006.

Virsa Systems
Virsa Systems is a company that develops enterprise risk management software. Virsa specializes in software that enables companies to comply with Sarbanes-Oxley, HIPAA, GLB, and other government regulations.
Date: April 2006.

2005

Callixa
Callixa is a developer of enterprise information integration software. Their distributed query processing technology enables developers to write a query that can be distributed among different databases and other data stores, gathering information and sending it back to the application in a single, unified response.
Date: December 2005.

Khimetrics
Khimetrics, Inc. is a leading provider of customer demand management solutions for retail, financial services, and consumer packaged goods (CPG) industries. As the customer demand experts, Khimetrics helps retailers synchronize their merchandising strategies with customer demand to increase sales and profit margins while improving competitive positioning.
Date: November 2005.

Transact In Memory
Transact In Memory (TIM) is a provider of memory-centric, lightweight, relational database solutions. TIM’s patent-pending technologies enable real-time acquisition, analysis, and archiving of data, even in the most update- and search-intensive environments.
Date: November 2005.

Triversity
Triversity is a point-of-sale (POS) software solution provider. Their system offers POS loss prevention, inventory management, as well as store back-office and in-store customer service solutions in addition to an array of POS data. These solutions are highly complementary to SAP’s existing retail solution offering.
Date: September 2005.

Lighthammer Software
Lighthammer Software is a supplier of enterprise manufacturing intelligence and collaborative manufacturing software. Their web-based software allows monitoring and managing operations at manufacturing facilities.
Date: June 2005.

DCS Quantum
DCS Quantum is a provider of vehicle dealer management systems. Their solution is designed to enable vehicle importers, distributors, dealer groups, and independent dealers to consolidate and improve sales and service processes and to achieve more effective collaboration.
Date: February 2005.

TomorrowNow
TomorrowNow was a PeopleSoft support and maintenance vendor. It was shut down in 2008.
Date: January 2005.

2004

A2i
A2i develops and markets xCat, a platform for product content management and cross-media catalog publishing. The Data Management A2i xCat system is an enterprise-class catalog system designed to allow a user to easily build, structure, and query very large catalogs.
Date: July 2004.

iLytix Systems
iLytix Systems develops a reporting and budgeting tool. The tool, called XL Reporter, helps companies pull together business reports and budgets that can be viewed in Microsoft's Excel spreadsheet software.
Date: January 2004.

SAP Systems Integration (SAP SI)
SAP SI provides systems integration services.
Date: March 2004 / October 2005

2003

DCW Software
SAP takes over a share of DCW, vendor of SME-focused software.
Date: September 2003.

2002

TopManage Financial Solutions
TopManage provides accounting and business management software solutions for small and medium enterprises (SME).
Date: March 2002.

2001

TopTier Software
TopTier develops portal software and integration products.
Date: March 2001.

2000

OFEK-Tech
OFEK-Tech is a company specializing in Warehouse Management and Control.

1998

Campbell Software
Campbell Software is a provider of workforce management (WFM) and personal time and attendance recording software.

1997

Kiefer & Veittinger
Kiefer & Veittinger is a sales force automation software company. 

1994

Dacos Software
Dacos is a software provider for the retail industry.

1991

Steeb Anwendungssysteme
Steeb provides consulting services. In 2011, it was merged with All for One.

October 21, 2026
Q3 2026 Financial Results
Christian Klein, CEO

“Q3 was an outstanding quarter, with current cloud backlog up 26% at constant currencies. Our Autonomous Enterprise strategy is not just resonating, it is being adopted. Our customers are investing in the technology behind it – from the cloud and data foundation to our Business AI. They see that Joule Work makes the business case for their transformation more attractive than ever.”

Dominik Asam, CFO

“For the first time, SAP crossed €10 billion in total quarterly revenue and €3 billion of non-IFRS operating profit, reflecting the strength and scalability of our business model. Our disciplined approach to cost management, paired with continued cloud momentum, demonstrates our ability to grow both the top and bottom line at the same time.”

At a Glance

  • Current cloud backlog of €24.1 billion, up 28% and up 26% at constant currencies

  • Cloud revenue up 26% and up 25% at constant currencies

  • Cloud ERP Suite revenue up 29% and up 28% at constant currencies

  • Total revenue up 13% and up 12% at constant currencies

  • IFRS operating profit up 18%, non-IFRS operating profit up 18%, both at nominal and constant currencies

  • SAP updates its 2026 cloud revenue and cloud and software revenue outlook
